A procedure for the seismic analysis of underground tunnels using recorded free-field earthquakes based on the 2.5D finite/infinite element approach is presented. The near and far fields of the half space are modeled by finite and infinite elements, respectively. Using the 1D wave theory, the nodal force and displacement on the near-field boundary are computed for each spectral frequency of the earthquake. Then, equivalent seismic forces are computed for the near-field boundary for the earthquake spectrum. By assuming the soil-tunnel system to be uniform along the tunnel axis, the 2.5D approach can account for the wave transmission along the tunnel axis, which reduces to the 2D case for infinite transmission velocity. The horizontal and vertical components of the 1999 Chi-Chi Earthquake (TCU068) are adopted as the free-field motions in the numerical analysis. The maximal stresses and distribution patterns of the tunnel section under the P- and SV-waves are thoroughly studied by the 2.5D and 2D approaches, which should prove useful to the design of underground tunnels.

Emergency Department Operations Management
Emergency Department (ED) overcrowding is a long-standing and serious issue confronting many countries and cities. ED overcrowding can lead to numerous grievous consequences, including prolonged pain and suffering, patients' dissatisfaction, and, most importantly, delay in the delivery of appropriate medical care to emergency patients. In this project, we apply OR techniques (analytical modeling and systems simulation) and data analytics for analyzing and improving ED operations in Hong Kong.

Medical appointment scheduling is a challenging problem for hospitals and clinics due to the multi-dimensional stochasticity in practice, such as patient no-shows, patient unpunctuality, and non-deterministic service times. In this project, we developed a stochastic mixed-integer linear programming model to optimize medical appointment schedules.

Digitisation of Human Body Motion
for Garment Production
Professor Norman C. TIEN
Chair Professor
Department of Electrical
and Electronic Engineering
Garment production is a laborious process that relies primarily on manual operations. Smart robots are set to play a vital role in future automations and assist human workers with repetitive and/or high-risk tasks. To achieve interactive human-robot collaborations, robots need to learn and understand how humans work and thus a cost-effective means of digitising manual operations is of the essence. In this project, we aim at developing an innovative approach to high-fidelity, real-time full-body motion capture for garment workers without using specialty cameras.
Real-time motion tracking for human-robot interaction research
電視
Professor Tien is the Chair Professor of Microsystems Technology of HKU and Managing Director of the Centre for Transformative Garment Production. He is an expert in MEMS technology and robotics.
https://www.transgp.hk
info@transgp.hk
Robotic assistance in garment handling
Novelty of the project
Existing methods for 3D full-body motion capture utilise either multiple high-end industrial cameras or RGB cameras equipped with depth sensors, which are costly and usually require sophisticated setups. As regards human pose estimation, most works mainly estimate the 3D coordinates of each joint of the human body, neglecting the fact that it is the rotation of skeletal bones that result in different human poses. Our approach treats a human body as a kinematic tree and learns to infer the rotation of each skeletal bone. Using monocular videos as input, our algorithm incorporates the knowledge learned from a large-scale dataset and leverages a fusion strategy to integrate both human body and hand poses so that a pose estimation with improved correspondence with the actual human body can be realised.
Computer modelling and simulation of human motion
Benefit to the community
Besides virtual reality and 3D gaming that first come to the spectators' mind, the developed technology will facilitate human-robot collaborations in the labour-intensive garment industry, where the motions and activities of human workers are digitally captured via the system and analysed for motion intents in order to predict workers' subsequent movements using artificial intelligence. With such advanced capability, robotic assistance can be effectively implemented that enhances the productivity and safety of various production and handling tasks. This technology using a commodity digital camera may also find promising applications in monitoring the elderly for enabling ageing-in-place and evaluation of postures and movements during rehabilitation.
Robot working collaboratively with a human operator on a sewing task
About the Centre
The project represents a part of the large-scale research programmes of the Centre for Transformative Garment Production, which is jointly formed by HKU and Tohoku University, Japan to tackle real-world technical problems facing the garment production industry. The Centre has been admitted to the AIR@InnoHK Research Cluster under the funding support of Innovation and Technology Commission of the HKSAR Government.

Detection and Diagnostics of Airborne Viruses
Professor Anderson H.C. SHUM
Professor
Department of Mechanical Engineering
A lot of diseases can be transmitted via airborne agents, such as viruses spreading through droplets. The concentrations of these airborne agents are usually too low in the environment and it has created difficulties for the current detection instruments available in the market. We aim to fill this gap by developing new technologies to enhance detection and diagnostics of airborne viruses.
電視
Professor Shum is the professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering of HKU and Centre Director of Advanced Biomedical Instrumentation Centre His research interests are Emissions, Self- condensed matter physics, Microfluidics, Emulsion-templated materials, Nano-microfluidics, Drug delivery, Colloidity applications and Food applications.
www.ABIC.hk
info@ABIC.hk
The collaboration between HKU and the Centre will facilitate the design of devices and instruments that may create global impact in healthcare
The Centre focuses on developing Affordable Screening Tests, Personalised Companion Diagnostics, Strategic Therapeutic Approaches, and Advanced Medical Device Components
Novelty of the project
The development of new devices and instrumentations is based on a novel physicochemical approach. They will be able to (1) detect the airborne viruses at lower virus concentration; and (2) identify the viruses in a short period of time.
In the future, zero contact with secretions could be done during the virus detection process. It not only reduces the chance of infection for medical staff, but also alleviates the discomfort of participants during the test.
Benefit to the community
Airborne diseases have been demonstrated to spread quickly in indoor environments. Our techniques can be potentially developed into instruments for environmental monitoring, which is an important requirement for controlling outbreaks. For example, these instruments can be deployed and distributed in indoor environments to alert the occupants of potential presence of infected persons. This will facilitate the identification of potential group of infected persons and the control of spread of diseases.
It hopefully will help contribute to addressing future pandemics.
About the Centre
The Advanced Biomedical Instrumentation Centre, set up with the funding support from the Health@InnoHK initiative by the Innovation and Technology Commission of the HKSAR Government, fosters collaboration among top-notch scientists engineers and clinicians. The Centre is a collaboration between HKU and the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences at Harvard University, and the goal is to develop next-generation and low-cost medical instrumentation. The research and development themes include (1) Affordable Screening Tests, (2) Personalised Companion Diagnostics, (3) Strategic Therapeutic Approaches, and (4) Advanced Medical Device Components.

A set of mechanical, control, sensory, and AI technologies is being developed which includes:

Benefit to the community
One of the alarming consequences of the growing ageing population is the fast decline of functional capacity that older elderly experience. While constrained physical and cognitive abilities leave many older adults dependent, most of them prefer to continue living in their homes rather than moving into nursing homes. With the intelligent walking assistance and falling protection from our walker, an active, independent and quality life of the ageing population is supported, which can not only slow overall functional decline, but also reduce health care costs by delaying premature institutionalization.

電視
Professor Cheng's main research area is data science. He is specialized in big graphs, knowledge bases, social networks, and uncertain databases.
https://www.hincare.hku.hk
ckcheng@cs.hku.hk
Novelty of the project
HINCare is the first intelligent timebanking system that enables timebanking for multiple NGOs in Hong Kong. Traditional elderly care and timebanking systems often do not use big data in the decision process. Our project uses novel HIN and AI technologies to perform helper-elder matching. While most existing solutions support a single organization only, our cloud-based system can be used by multiple organizations. The gigantic HIN for storing the relationship information of elderly people, helpers, and NGOs will be useful to gerontology researchers and policymakers to extract insights about social behaviors, thereby making better decisions.
Benefit to the community
1. The HINCare platform is now serving more than 2,000 elderly people and helpers in 5 NGOs in Hong Kong. The NGOs have reflected that HINCare streamlines their processes in timebanking, increases the effectiveness and efficiency in administering volunteering services. Some more NGOs will use HINCare to support timebanking projects in the next two year, benefiting more than 5,000 users.
2. Big Data Research: The data collected such as the pattern of the services required, locations and frequency of services, elders-volunteers matching, ratings of services, are very useful to gerontology researchers and policymakers.

Unravelling How

Transmitted
Professor Yuguo Li
Chair Professor
Department of Mechanical Engineering
How is the emerging new SARS-CoV-2 transmitted? This has been one of the major challenges for effective intervention since the COVID-19 pandemic emerged in late 2019.
Following our continuous environmental studies of infection since 2003 SARS epidemics, our team immediately explored our long-held hypothesis that short-range inhalation transmission might predominate the spread of most respiratory infection.

Professor Li is the Chair Professor of Building Environment at HKU. His research interests include city climate development, environment studies of infection and indoor environment. Novelty of the project
1. Our work provided the essential probable evidence for recognizing the airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2 by the health community in July 2020.
2. We identified the chimney effect in the drainage stack explained more than 10 vertical COVID-19 outbreaks in Hong Kong.
3. We identified short-range inhalation transmission of SARS-CoV-2, which has been recognized by World Health Organization (WHO) and U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (UC CDC).
4. We redefined transmission routes as inhalation, spray and touch, which has been accepted by US CDC.

Benefit to the community
1. Recognition of airborne transmission paves the way for improving ventilation, e.g. in dine-in restaurants in Hong Kong, and for specifying maximum classroom capacity for each of HKU classrooms.
2. Recognition of short-range inhalation transmission calls for the need of wearing N95 masks by health care workers.
3. New understanding of vertical outbreaks shows the urgent need for improving and monitoring drainage systems in high-rise housing.
4. The new concepts of aerosol inhalation, drop spray and surface touch promises easy communication for infection control of respiratory infection.

for SARS-CoV-2 Virus
Professor Tong ZHANG

The sewage testing tool for SARS-CoV-2 virus was invented by an inter-disciplinary team led by Professor Tong Zhang, from the Environmental Microbiome Engineering and Biotechnology Laboratory of the Department of Civil Engineering of the Faculty of Engineering.
電視
Extraction of SARS-CoV-2 RNA from
sewage
Detection of SARS-CoV-2 using RT-qPCR
Professor Zhang is the Chair Professor in Department of Civil Engineering, HKU. His researches focus on the environment-microbiome-health dimensions, including studies of antibiotic and antibiotic resistance genes, microbiome-based biotechnology, environmental biotechnology, environmental bioinformatics, and biological wastewater treatment.
https://mite.hku.hk
zhangt@hku.hk
Novelty of the project
Firstly, we invented a two-step separation method and used detections of two gene segments of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. In one case, it enabled the successful detection of one COVID-19 patient out of 56,000 people from their aggregated sewage sample. Secondly, we developed a compact auto-sampler that can be easily mounted underneath the existing sewerage manhole covers to collect the sewage sample automatically, thus minimizing the impacts on ground-level public activities. Thirdly, a territory-wide sewage surveillance system has been well established in Hong Kong through close collaboration between an interdisciplinary research team of environmental microbiology and public health from the University of Hong Kong and the Government of the Hong Kong SAR, including the Environment Bureau, the Food and Health Bureau, the Drainage Services Department and the Environmental Protection Department.
An overview of the sewage surveillance for COVID-19 in Hong Kong
Benefit to the community
This tool helps track hidden transmission chain in community, and it was successfully implemented to uncover more than 50 hidden COVID-19 cases in local community in Hong Kong by triggering in government compulsory testing. This new invention has now been transferred to commercial labs for routine monitoring of COVID-19 re-emergence for over five million residents. It now serves as a powerful management tool to fight COVID-19 by providing early warning signals of silent virus transmission with over 200 samples collected every week from 112 stationary monitoring sites that cover 5.3 million people living in the city.

Novelty of the project
The developed highly porous, multifunctional, and nanostructured filters consist of numerous functional nanofibers fabricated by electrospinning for high-efficiency water and air purification. The major innovation features of the filter include: 1) nanostructured multifunctional porous filters for effective air filtration (e.g., >99% removal of 0.3 µm particles, indicating excellent efficiency for eliminating nano-sized air pollutants including bioaerosols and viruses); 2) rapid water filters that are electricity-free, chemical-free, compact, and with high removal efficiency (e.g., >99.9% for heavy metals and >99.99999% for bacteria); 3) reusable filter designs for improved sustainability.

Benefit to the community
The project will create great benefits to the communities which include:
1. Meeting urgent public demand for clean air amid COVID-19. Our air filters offer long lasting, highly efficient, and sustainable air filtration to address the critical challenges on air quality during COVID-19.
2. Providing clean drinking water for people with urgent needs. Our water filter technology enables instant provision of clean water for urgent needs, featuring rapid water purification and high-efficiency removal without the need of electricity and chemical addition.
3. Promoting environmental sustainability. The reusable features of our water and air filters extend their lifespan and effectively reduce the generation of waste from exhausted filters.

Characteristics of fluidic processor
Novelty of the project
Contamination-free: Fluid loss with the processor is only 0.5% of that of the available technology. We
consumed US$20 billion of plastics annually to handle fluids because of inter-sample contamination
caused by fluids retention. The fluidic processor can potentially replace disposable plastics and ease
environmental strain.
A wide spectrum of fluids: The new processor is compatible with nearly all liquids in biomedical and
chemical industry. Its maneuverable fluid volume can be from 1000 µl to tiny droplets at 0.001 µl, i.e.
about 0.02% of the volume of blood in a mosquito bite, which is 100 times smaller than that
manipulated by its electrical counterpart.
Toward commercial products: The key technology of the device is a three-layer photo-responsive
platform, costing only about US$50. With a thickness of only 1mm, it is portable and easy to handle.

Intelligent Mobile Robots for
UVC based Disinfection
Professor Ning Xi
Chair Professor
Department of Industrial and
Manufacturing Systems Engineering
Current surface disinfection methods include spraying chemicals or using UV light. However, it is difficult to directly spray liquid chemicals on surfaces due to the threat of negative environmental impacts and possible damage and contamination to various surfaces such as books and food packages. Currently, UV based disinfection lights are either wall mounted or operate on mobile bases. Moreover, they are often positioned metres away from surfaces that require disinfection.
電視
Disinfecting books in a public library
Disinfecting exercise machines in a public gym
Professor Xi is the Chair Professor of Robotics and Automation in Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering. His research interests focus on robotics, intelligent control, automation, micro/nano manufacturing, nano sensors and devices, and intelligent control and systems.
https://www.mse.hku.hk/people/n-xi
nnxing@hku.hk
Novelty of the project
The disinfection robot was developed based on the results of multi-year R&D on automatic robot programming, autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance, sensor-based robot control, and novel drives and structures. It also provides a convenient and cost-effective solution to fight against the pandemic.
In order to achieve effective disinfection within a short period of time, studies have shown that UV light must be centimetres away from a surface as its strength decays significantly when being transmitted through the air. In response to this issue, the UV based surface disinfection robot can disinfect selected areas by bringing the UV light source centimetres away from surfaces to achieve effective and efficient disinfection within seconds. Additionally, the robot can autonomously navigate in crowded areas such as hotels lobbies, gyms, and libraries to conduct disinfection.
Benefit to the community
COVID-19 has been devastating on a global scale, and therefore preventing its spread is an essential step towards suppressing the virus. Many studies show that people can become infected easily by coming into contact with contaminated surfaces. Moreover, the COVID-19 virus can be viable for a number of days on many surfaces including plastic, stainless steel, and paper. This has proven to be a major challenge for public facilities such as public libraries, restrooms, sports arenas, and transport facilities. Hence, it is essential for surfaces often used by the public to be decontaminated effectively. The technologies developed in this project have wide applications such as painting in constructions, surface treatment and inspection in manufacturing and maintenance, and cleaning in property management.
Achievement of the project
Testing trials at Public Library with Electrical and Mechanical Services Department.

with Force Self-decoupling
Dr Jia PAN
Assistant Professor
Department of Computer Science
Human skin can sense subtile changes of both normal and shear forces as well as perceive stimulus with finer resolution than the average spacing between mechanoreceptors. By contrast, existing tactile sensors for robotic applications are inferior, lacking both accurate force decoupling and proper spatial resolution. This project aims at developing skin-like soft tactile sensors based on principles of magnetic fields.

Novelty of the project
In this project, we demonstrate a soft tactile sensor with self-decoupling and super-resolution abilities by designing a sinusoidally magnetized flexible film (with the thickness ~0.5 millimeters), whose deformation can be detected by a Hall sensor according to the change of magnetic flux densities under external forces. The sensor can accurately measure the normal force and the shear force with a single unit and achieve a 60-fold super-resolved accuracy enhanced by deep learning. By mounting our sensor at the fingertip of a robotic gripper we show that our robots can accomplish challenging tasks like stably grasping fragile objects under external disturbance and threading a needle via teleoperation.
Benefit to the community
This research provides new insight into tactile sensor design and could be beneficial to various applications in robotics field, such as adaptive grasping, dexterous manipulation, and human-robot interaction.
Compared with the traditional tactile sensors that are either mechanically decoupled (using multiple sensing units) or decoupled by data-fitting methods (using complicated models), our sensor is able to measure both the normal and shear forces in a decoupled way, which dramatically simplifies the sensor structure and the calibration process, and is thus more suitable to be used in practical applications than other sensors that are either complex to fabricate and calibrate or not robust for practical usage.

2-DAY BEGINNER WORKSHOP:
ROBOT CONTROL — FIRMWARE
Firmware is the software program in MCU (micro controller unit) to control the actuators such as servos and motors, and sensors of a robot. It is a challenge to develop a good firmware as MCU is not powerful as computer CPU. As MCU program runs in single thread model, programming techniques are required to efficiently coordinate each module (sensor or actuator) to avoid them from blocking each other. In this two-day workshop, you will learn the essential knowledge on writing firmware and apply what you have learnt to write the firmware for a wheel driven robot - WheeBot.
HKU Engineering students and InnoHub members preferably with C/C++ programming knowledge, are welcome to join.

Innovations in
studying the past with technology
Technology is increasingly important in studying humanities topics such
as archaeology. For examples, when we study the materials left behind
by the past societies, such as their architecture, pottery or animal
bones from meals, the complex data is digitalized to capture
information about the space, shape, decoration and materials to
facilitate our study of the human past.
HKU helps lead a collaborative fieldwork project in Armenia every
summer where we are excavating a fortress with 3,000 years ago. This
field project is a laboratory for experimenting with various technologies
including drone-based Lidar, 3D scanning of spaces and objects,
computer vision, machine learning, databases and many other
technologies, in the hot and dusty field conditions.
In this workshop, we will introduce some of the past engineering
experiments and their technological difficulties. All participants can join
us in developing new technological solutions that can facilitate our field
works in the future. Participating students may also get a chance to join
us in Armenia next summer!
Date: September 22, 2022 (Thu)
Time: 3:00-4:00pm
Venue: Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing
Speaker:
Dr Peter Cobb
Assistant Professor, School of Humanities, HKU
Dr Cobb teaches courses on archaeological methods and theories and the
archaeology of the ancient world, including experiential learning classes
abroad. He has conducted archaeological fieldwork in Laos, Armenia, and
Turkey, and is currently the director of the Ararat Plain Southeast
Archaeological Project (APSAP) in collaboration with the Armenian Institute
of Archaeology and Ethnography. His research focuses on the Late Bronze
and Iron Ages (ca 1600-100 BCE) of the Eastern Mediterranean and ancient
Southwest Asia (aka the Ancient Near East). Dr Cobb is a specialist in the
analysis of ancient ceramics and in digital humanities (DH). He holds a joint
appointment with the Human Communication, Development, and
Information Sciences academic unit of the Faculty of Education.

NFT BUSINESS MODEL:
QUICK WIN AND LONG-TERM STRATEGY
NFT is not rocket science. The blockchain-based data ownership management technology appears to have made the statement 'Data is the new oil' come true literally, mainly via digital art. Dapper Labs, the creator of one of the first NFT games Cryptokitties, has received a USD7.6 billion valuation in late 2021; meanwhile, NFTs has generated over USD23 billion in trading volume in 2021. Daily NFT trading volume, however, has dropped 80% on the NFT-marketplace OpenSea last month. In this workshop, we are going to discuss whether it has been a hype and how we should plan the business and investment strategies towards a highly speculative market. We will also explore how you could make the best use of your creativity and knowledge in developing NFT-technology-based projects that bring positive impact and create tangible and intangible value.

ONLINE WORKSHOP
From hospital-centric to human-centric:
Personalized wearables for digital healthcare
The soaring population aging, the quarantine and the shortage of medical instrumentations are demanding decentralized medical technologies that can enable remote and personalized healthcare. Wearable technologies are the protagonists. Emerging wearable devices include, but are not limited to, smartwatches, smart clothing, smart glasses, smart jewelry, and wearable cameras. Some of these wearables can already measure vital signals such as heart rates, breathing rates and blood pressure. Moving forward, next-generation wearables are expected to enable on-demand blood tests and continuous recording of our electrophysiological signals for disease screening and monitoring. However, several challenges remain.
In this workshop, the speaker will describe how wearable technologies are impacting our healthcare systems, how to develop a wearable device, how we can address the most pressing challenges with transdisciplinary biomedical engineering approaches, and finally, how Biomedical Engineering can ultimately improve the human health.

Speaker:
Dr Shiming Zhang
Dr Shiming Zhang is currently an Assistant Professor at the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) of the University of Hong Kong (HKU), leading the wearable, intelligent and soft electronics (WISE) research group. ONLINE WORKSHOP
Crafting the multiverse of cells
to reshape healthcare
In the past 10 years at HKU Engineering, Professor Kevin Tsia and his team have developed a suite of optical imaging technologies that generated brand new views and understanding of the living biological cells. They include: capturing high-resolution motion picture of the swift-flying brain signals; visualising the inner workings of cells and organisms in 3D; and detecting rare cancer cells in millions of blood cells. In this workshop, Professor Tsia will describe how and why these technologies, when cautiously synergised with artificial intelligence, can be used for generating and analyzing all the unprecedented data relevant to the millions and millions of cells. It is essentially to create a "multiverse" of cells from which we could unlock the previously unknown information for supporting new biological discovery, and new-generation of cost-effective clinical diagnosis.
Speaker:
Professor Kevin Tsia
Kevin Tsia is currently a Professor in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering and the Program Director of the Biomedical Engineering Program at the University of Hong Kong. His research interest covers a broad range of subject matters including ultra-fast optical imaging for imaging flow cytometry and high-speed in-vivo brain imaging, bioinformatics approaches for single-cell analysis. He is currently the HK Research Grants Council (RGC) Research Fellow (2020). He received Early Career Award 2012-2013 by RGC in Hong Kong. He also received the Outstanding Young Research Award 2015 at HKU as well as 14th Chinese Science and Technology Award for Young Scientists in 2016. He is author or coauthor of over 200 journal publications conference papers and book chapters. He holds 4 granted and 6 pending US patents on ultrafast optical imaging technologies. He is a co-founder of start-up company commercializing the high speed microscopy technology for cancer screening and treatment monitoring applications.

within a virtual world. In this workshop, the speaker will talk about what are digital
assets and NFTs, and also how they are used in the metaverse.

Survival guide for COVID-19:
Why ventilation matters?
Although airborne transmission of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has already been acknowledged by leading health authorities, no existing standard for building ventilation yet considers the need to control respiratory infection. The speaker shall explain why outdoor has a lower infection risk than indoor, and why poor ventilation can worsen both short- and long-range inhalation. The speaker shall present a new equal CO2 exposure method to derive a set of minimum ventilation rates and associated maximum CO2 concentrations in indoor settings with various activity levels (rest, light-, moderate- and heavy-exercise) and breathing modes (breathing, speaking, singing and loudly speaking). BUILD SMART – INNOVATION IN CONSTRUCTION
2:00-3:00pm · April 28, 2021 (Wednesday) · Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing or via ZOOM
Construction and infrastructure make significant contributions to economic growth and social development. In Hong Kong, the annual construction output will reach HK$300billion in the coming years. However, the construction industry in many economies face significant challenges such as labour shortages, an ageing workforce and cost escalation, which hamper the enhancement of productivity and sustainability. Various innovative approaches have been developed, spearheaded by modular integrated construction (MiC), coupled with the adoption of many smart technologies such as AI, IoT, VR, robot, Digital Twin, etc. This workshop aims to systematically explore the knowledge, theory, and technology solutions of innovation in construction and infrastructure development. The workshop will first define the key concepts within their theoretical contexts. We will then examine the smart technologies adopted in construction with demonstration cases. Innovations and technologies will be illustrated using various real-life projects. Metaphorically, MiC acts as an aircraft carrier to drive smart technologies which act as fighter aircrafts, in return, to safeguard and empower MiC in transforming the industry towards sustained success. The workshop will also explore the prospective development of innovation by sharing the latest research and development led by CiCID and MiC Lab of HKU.

Problems
How can we teach kids about AI in an hands-on and intuitive way?
How can we make this technology relevant to them so they would care?
Potential Solution
By developing and testing MEW, a node based "AI as a materiel" visual coding software built on top of Scratch, this project aims to explore how and why we might support kids to learn AI.

MEW provides an intuitive visual interface for beginners to start making simple AI projects.
Methodology
Development
The software was developed in 2 stages:
Stage 1: Minimum viable product version of the software built with HTML, CSS and JS. Less framework for rapid iteration. Limited Scratch integration.
Stage 2: A more polished version built with React. Integrated directly into Scratch by creating a fork of the Scratch GUI repo and rebuilding all the features from stage 1. Many important new features that were requested in stage 1 testing were also added.
Playtesting Workshops
Testing and development were interlaced to discover problems early and validate design decisions.

SUSTAINABLE WEEDING SOLUTION
INNOGROW
Abstract
Sustainable farming is gaining traction in Asia to address weed challenges that hinder crop growth. Traditional weed control methods often rely on toxic chemicals that are unsustainable in the long term, negatively impacting soil health and reducing fertility. Therefore, there is an urgent need for innovative weed elimination methods that do not depend on these conventional solutions.
We propose a compact, versatile weed-killing device that easily attaches to various farming equipment, such as harrows, tractors, or ATVs. Utilizing an affordable camera and advanced computer vision, the device accurately detects weeds, which are then targeted by a laser based on gathered positional data. Housed in a lightweight unit powered by a compact processing unit, it ensures speed and efficiency.
Our innovative device offers a cost-effective solution for small farmers, enabling effective weed management without chemicals. This approach enhances crop yields, improves the quality of life for both farmers and consumers, and promotes environmental sustainability, supporting the transition to more sustainable farming practices.

HEARTFUL: DEVELOPING A COUNSELLING
LLM VIA API AND PROMPT ENGINEERING
Kim Ian, Wang Liheng Grace, Dr Kevin Wu, Dr Lei Yang
Introduction
Large language models (LLMs) play a central role in our daily lives, and its integration has revolutionized processes
This has been used in many applications such as customer support, education, with some even using it for chatbots for mental health.
However, a shortcoming in the use of such models for counselling purposes is that, while it is able to simulate empathy through language, the responses are safe but generic that ignore specific nuances or factors (i.e. an inability to read between the lines). It is thereby unable to provide true "genuineness" specific to a client.
We therefore introduce our model Heartful to overcome such limitations, where it is created to provide remedial counselling services with psychotherapeutic concepts in mind.
Future directions include the offering of tools such as grounding exercises, cognitive reframing prompts, and behavior planning, while maintaining a supportive, non-judgmental tone. We thus discuss the impact of AI on counselling techniques.

OUR SCIENTIFIC PRINCIPLE
We engineered E.coli with a novel light-harvesting system (NPM) inspired by
photosynthetic bacteria. By embedding NuoK (electron transporter), PufL
(reaction center), and MgP (chlorophyll analog), we created a light-dependent
electron chain. This system uses methanol as an electron donor to produce
formaldehyde and NADH—key precursors for hydrogen synthesis.
METABOLIC ENGINEERING MASTERY
GSH Overproduction: Knocking out gpmA halts competing pathways, while
gshA/gshB overexpression floods cells with glutathione. This traps formaldehyde
as S-hydroxymethylglutathione, driving its conversion to formate.
FHL Hyperactivation: Derepressing fhlA (activator) and removing iscR/hycA (inhibitors)
unleashes the FHL complex. This enzyme system splits formate into H2 and CO2 with
industrial-scale efficiency.

ONLINE WORKSHOP
Digital twin is a virtual model of an object or system that spans its lifecycle. With its real-time IoT data, stimulations, machine learning and AI applications, we can have timely feedback to optimize performance of the object/system, as well as facilitate our decision-making. In this workshop, the speakers will introduce the concept of digital twin and its applications in the real world. ONLINE WORKSHOP
Mysteries of NFTs
and how they shape
the Metaverse
Mar 23 (Wed)
3:30-4:30pm
Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) is the most popular form of digital asset in the last two years. NFTs can be associated with digital art, music, or in-game asset. Recently, NFTs have emerged as a foundation for the internal infrastructure and economy of the metaverse. One interesting example is the use of NFTs to buy virtual land in the metaverse, which worth USD$3.2M. These virtual spaces use NFTs, as opposed to a physical deed, to reflect ownership of specific locations within a virtual world. In this workshop, the speaker will talk about what are digital assets and NFTs, and also how they are used in the metaverse.

BUILD SMART – INNOVATION IN CONSTRUCTION
2:00-3:00pm · April 28, 2021 (Wednesday) · Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing or via ZOOM
Construction and infrastructure make significant contributions to economic growth and social development. In Hong Kong, the annual construction output will reach HK$300billion in the coming years. However, the construction industry in many economies face significant challenges such as labour shortages, an ageing workforce and cost escalation, which hamper the enhancement of productivity and sustainability. Various innovative approaches have been developed, spearheaded by modular integrated construction (MiC), coupled with the adoption of many smart technologies such as AI, IoT, VR, robot, Digital Twin, etc. This workshop aims to systematically explore the knowledge, theory, and technology solutions of innovation in construction and infrastructure development. The workshop will first define the key concepts within their theoretical contexts. We will then examine the smart technologies adopted in construction with demonstration cases. Innovations and technologies will be illustrated using various real-life projects. Metaphorically, MiC acts as an aircraft carrier to drive smart technologies which act as fighter aircrafts, in return, to safeguard and empower MiC in transforming the industry towards sustained success. The workshop will also explore the prospective development of innovation by sharing the latest research and development led by CICID and MiC Lab of HKU.

SOCIAL WORKER INTERACTIVE TRAINING CHATBOT
SWITCH
BY INNOVATION WING & DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WORK
BACKGROUND OF PROJECT
Role-playing is one method used in training social work students.
Using a real client is risky.
Using professional counselors as clients is costly.
The students have to role-play the client ineffective
That's why chatbot comes into play!
However, existing chatbots lack the ability to adapt their openness or attitude during conversations, making them appear unrealistic.
We propose a realistic role-playing client with systematic behavior shifting
1
TECHNIQUE CLASSIFICATION
To evaluate social work students' conversational skills and performance, our system classifies key techniques used by students during interactions with the AI client.
Automated Conversation Classification:
Classifies dialogues into 22 key categories defined by social work experts.
Uses annotated client-social worker conversations as training data.
High-Accuracy Classification Methods:
Tests multiple approaches to optimize results, including in-context learning & supervised fine-tuning.
Actionable Feedback:
Generates a technique distribution report to pinpoint strengths/weaknesses.
2
OPENNESS ADJUSTMENT
Openness level is introduced to simulate the real counseling sessions, which clients starting reserved but gradually becoming more willing to share as trust builds.
Openness adjustment enables students to practice:
Early-stage resistance: Handling guarded or defensive responses.
Gradual disclosure: Encouraging trust through active listening and validation.
Openness Adjustment Mechanism (Guided by Social Work Experts)
Conversation progress: Openness increases with rounds of dialogue, like natural trust-building.
Student skills: Use of active listening, validation, and etc. influences the rate of disclosure.
DEMO
3
ROLE-PLAYING AGENT
The constructed prompt which will be fed to the model consists of 2 parts.
1. Client's profile and client's background story – provided by social worker, each with goals that students need to achieve
2. Openness prompt – informing the model how much and helpful it should respond
The prompt is designed and developed based on social workers' feedback.
Technique Usage
[unreadable]
FUTURE WORK
Our project will be expanded to incorporate many features, for more effective and engaging for social worker training.
Emotional depth: another adjustable dimension additional to openness level.
Speech to speech interaction: Voice input and output capabilities simulating verbal communication with real-life clients, with possible extension to the use of voice tone and pitch to enhance emotional realism
Improved accuracy: The chatbot will be progressively refined to provide more realistic answers, especially in a range of diverse scenarios.
Performance Evaluation: add features including conversation summaries and a performance analytics dashboard.

Blind quadrupedal magic
Allowing legged robots to walk on different terrains without using visual data
Referenced paper for this project:
"DreamWeQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning"
Final Year Project by Soogon Kim
In this project, our team aimed to enable a quadruped robot to navigate various terrains without relying on visual input. To achieve this, we studied a paper called "DreamWeQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning" and utilized Beta Variational Autoencoder with a policy network to help robots interpret their surrounding environment using past proprioceptive data.
How it works:
the Encoder receives 5 proprioceptive past observations that can be obtained inside robot's internal sensor. The , the encoder produces a vector "z" that represents robot's imagination of the environmen. Finally, based on the vector z, the policy produces 12 angle joint values for the robot to move.

MOTIVATION
Challenges in Robotic Arm Adoption
Skill Gap: Most workers in traditional industries lack the programming skills needed to operate robotic arms.
Psychological Barrier: Employees often find robotic arms intimidating due to their complexity and the perception of losing control over tasks.
OVERVIEW
The system simplifies teleoperation using geometric constraints and error-tolerant design, enabling precise control while reducing user workload.
The CNC machine cleaning task, developed from the daily routine work of a local Public Transport Company (PTC) in Hong Kong, guides workers into the field of Robotics. Applying the proposed task, our solution makes teleoperation more intuitive, reliable, and user-friendly.
EE Trajectory
CNC Machine

METHOD
6-DoF Manipulation
Map movements from a 6-DoF controller to the robotic arm's end-effector for intuitive control.
Constraint Adaption
Align motions to geometric constraints (e.g., planes, straight lines) to reduce fatigue and ensure precision.
Intention Prediction
Predict user intentions and provide dynamic assistance to enhance human-robot interaction.

USER EXPERIENCE AND DISCUSSION
Bridging the Skill Gap:
Three PTC trainees tested our system and were able to clean CNC machine grooves independently after a brief introduction, without damaging the robotic arm. This demonstrates the system's effectiveness in simplifying robotic arm operation for non-experts.
Reducing Psychological Barriers:
Traditional teleoperation often leads to misalignment between user intention and robotic movement, causing unintended oscillations, collision risks, and a reduced sense of control. Our constraint-adaptive system improves usability by aligning movements with geometric constraints, minimizing manual adjustments, and enabling smoother, more intuitive operation.
FUTURE WORK
Expand Application Areas
Explore additional applications of the shared-autonomy system in fields such as industrial, healthcare, and creative arts.
Formal User Studies
Conduct formal user studies to gather more feedback and enhance the system based on real-world usage.

INFLUENCE OF DISINFECTANTS ON MICROBIAL WATER TREATMENT PROCESSES
By Chan Tsz Yu, Ben
Supervisor: Dr. G.Y.A
During the COVID-19 pandemic, the use of disinfectants has surged in order
spread of the virus. Many disinfectants will be sent to wastewater treatment plants
treatment before discharging back to the environment. Nevertheless, studies have shown
large amount of disinfectants can inhibit biological reactions during the wastewater treatment
process. The activated sludge process is particularly susceptible to disinfectants. Hence, this
study aims to investigate the inhibitory effects of two common active ingredients of
disinfectants, namely QACs and sodium hypochlorite, on the activated sludge process.
Quaternary Ammonium Compounds (QACs)
In general, QACs are considered as biodegradable in the activated sludge process since microorganisms in activated sludge utilize QACs as food and energy sources. Yet, studies have shown that high concentration of QACs can inhibit respiratory enzymes in activated sludge, causing activated sludge process to be interfered. Therefore, it is important to measure the percentage inhibition for each concentration of QACs to the activated sludge system.
Sodium Hypochlorite
Since sodium hypochlorite contains chlorine, it is sometimes added to activated sludge for chlorination and to control filamentous bulking problem. However, chlorination is not selective because it also affects COD removal rates and nitrification processes. Excessive sodium hypochlorite can affect the activities of activated sludge flora. Therefore, it is necessary to define the concentration of sodium hypochlorite that leads to inhibition of the activated sludge process.

I. Introduction
Hyporheic Exchanges (HE)
The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the region of saturated sediment surrounding a stream which connects surface water and groundwater flow. The overlying water with dissolved matters infiltrates into the HZ, stays there for some time and interacts with groundwater, and exfiltrates out of the HZ, resulting in hyporheic exchanges (HE). The HEs support physicochemical and biological reactions that are essential to river ecosystem functions.

Fig. 1. Hyporheic Exchange (Stonedahl et al., 2010)
River Restoration and HE
Most of the rivers are designed with narrow bottom section and large upper section of concrete streambed (Fig 2(a)). However, this design hinders HE which results in bad river eco-system. HE transports suspended and dissolved solutes such as nutrients, contaminants, organic carbon, and oxygen into the HZ. HZ creates a rich biocenosis composed of species that temporarily and permanently dwell there. In recent decades, more and more stream restoration projects involve the recovery of HE, however, effective guidance in restoring HE is still missing. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effectiveness of different key factors (e.g., stream discharge, slope, sinuosity and groundwater flow) in restoring HZ in a meandering channel with floodplain using flume experiments and numerical simulations.

Visible text:
LUMINO
INTRODUCTION
Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired. We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users.
Luminosite provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience.
Luminosite integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide: contesting awareness cognition.
We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone.
FEATURES
Advanced Navigation and Guidance System
Luminosite uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom-made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real-time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease.
In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual camera in the iPhone 7+ or later models, with ARKit, we can detect obstacles like walls in the 3D world. Besides, using kinematics information like the users' velocity and acceleration, we can provide warnings to the users in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents.
Latest Machine Learning Technology
Luminosite incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users, in particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the users with visual disability to recognize a wide variety of daily objects in their daily lives. On top of that, we took a step further by providing the relative position of the object to the users, so that they not only know "what" but also "where" in front of them.
We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, fluent conversations, just like how we communicate with other humans. Natural language processing analyzes the users' speech as a whole, providing accurate analysis of the users' intent even the user is speaking casually and not following any predefined format. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a virtual UI.

Application UI Refinement
Luminosite hopes to develop a new version of the application such that it not only caters the needs of the visually impaired, but also the general public. The ideas of providing haptic feedback to the user during the process of navigation is like providing crucial information to the user via the additional sense of feeling. It is different from current solutions which are distracting the users' attention from using their eyesight and hearing to recognize the situation on the road, which can be somewhat dangerous and thus not optimal.

INTRODUCTION
THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG

HKU LiTE
Research works in deep reinforcement learning have been emerging, however, only few of them actually demonstrate results on real physical agents. Duckietown Project provides an opportunity to properly benchmark the current state of the art of these methods as applied to real robotics system. The mission of our project is to democratise Artificial Intelligence (AI) and robotics research. Through this project, students gain tangible experience in a fun way in assembling self-driving robots and applying AI to the physical education platform developed by MIT.

Ziyang Dong1, Ziyan Guo1, Denny K.C. Fu1, Kit-Hang Lee1, Martin C.W. Leong1,

Overview
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques allow intra-operative monitoring of the ablation procedure during cardiovascular electrophysiology (EP). However, currently it is still challenging to carry out effective catheterization under MRI environment. We present an MR-safe robot for intra-cardiac EP intervention. The robot actuation features small hysteresis, effective force transmission and quick response. Experimental evaluation has verified its capability to precisely tele-manipulate a standard clinically used EP catheter.
Index Terms – Cardiac Electrophysiology, MR-safe Robot, Robot-assisted Intervention, MR-safe Actuation
Background
Motivation:
EP catheterization is an effective treatment for heart rhythm disorders, in which a catheter has to perform radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in the heart chamber (Fig.1);
Intra-operative MRI provides superior soft tissue contrast [1], which helps to access the lesion locations and ablation progress (Fig.2), so as to guide the catheter;
Robot can improve the accuracy of catheter manipulation for intra-cardiac EP intervention. Tele-operation of robot also eliminates the need of screens in MRI room.
Challenges:
Difficult to control the long (1.5m) and flexible EP catheter under the influence of beating heart chamber;
No ferromagnetic materials are allowed in MRI.

Method
Main features of the robotic catheter system:
Master-slave hydraulic actuation with low-friction rolling diaphragm seals are used to achieve MR-safe and precise actuation (Fig.4c & d );
All components of the robot slave part are made of MR-safe material and hydraulically actuated to minimize the EM interference; Catheter tip can be located by MR-based positional tracking in real-time to close the control loop (Fig.4a).

Results
Experimental validation:
MRI-compatibility test: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) loss <2%. Image artifact was negligible even when the robot is in motion (Fig.5);
Lab-based pulmonary vein isolation task: the teleoperated robot demonstrated high precision and sufficient workspace to create target lesions with an EP catheter (Fig.6);

Conclusion
The proposed MR-safe catheter robotic platform offers dexterous tele-manipulation of a cardiac catheter under intra-op MRI guidance. The high-efficient hydraulic transmission using rolling-diaphragm has demonstrated great potential of offering rapid but precise actuation under MRI, without adversely affecting the imaging quality.

What is it?
HKU-Denbot is a miniaturized surgical robotic manipulator for future robotic dentistry. With six Degree-of-Freedom design, the workspace of proposed manipulator could fully cover a human oral cavity dexterously while the whole body could be folded into a 50*50*50 cm³ suitcase, thus it could even be set up in private clinics where the space is severely constrained, especially at large cities like Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore and London.
Why Dental robot?
Over half the population in the world suffer from various oral diseases, and it will lead to lifelong pain and discomfort.
The Global Burden of Disease Study 2016
No. of people with oral diseases: 47.04%
No. of people without oral diseases: 52.46%
In developed cities like Hong Kong, there are shortages of medical professionals, while in rural areas, residents suffer from limited access to healthcare services. Therefore, it is expected HKU Denbot to be the solution for these problems.

SAPIENTIA ET VIRTUS
Evolving Human-Like Micromanagement in StarCraft II with Neuro-Evolution and Reinforcement Learning
STARCRAFT
Supervisor - Dr. Dirk Schneiders
Group Members - Fawad Masood Desmukh, Zain-Ul-Abidin
Introduction
Deliverables
Video games have always been a popular proving ground for artificial intelligence techniques. Traditional AI agents have relied on scripted, rule-based approaches that have several flaws. Recent breakthroughs have come through the application of novel machine learning approaches. In our project, we implement neuro-evolution using NEAT and reinforcement learning using Sarsa(lambda) to the real-time strategy game, StarCraft II, which is claimed to be the next "grand challenge" for artificial intelligence. Specifically, we apply it to micromanagement in StarCraft II which involves the small-scale precise control of individual army units
Applied Neuroevolution and Reinforcement Learning to SC2 micromanagement
Built frameworks for machine learning agents to interact with SC2
Generic training agents with helper functions to speed up development
Trained agents that successfully learnt starrant strategies for micro-scenarios
StarCraft II Map sets
Extensive Testing
Neuro-Evolution
Reinforcement Learning
Methodology
The neuroevolution approach combines neural networks with evolutionary algorithms. Through the NEAT algorithm, neural networks are dynamically generated and optimized across the training process. The NEAT algorithm in particular evolves both the weights as well as topology of the networks based on the fitness (performance) of the networks on the given tasks
Methodology
Reinforcement Learning aims to find a policy for an agent to maximise its reward in its environment. We applied the Sarsa(lambda) algorithm to micromanagement in SC2. It is a model-free, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit
Sarsa Agent
State – Self Unit Type, Unit Type of Closest Enemy, Distance to closest enemy, Scaled Relative Power, Is Together, Weapon Cooldown
Actions – Attack, Engage, Retreat, Scatter
NEAT-SC2 Framework
Open-Sourced framework developed to expedite the NEAT training and evaluation process for StarCraft II
Features
Launch configurable StarCraft II games through PySC2
Launch NEAT trainings fully configurable through the command line
Visualize training process
Checkpointing to pause and resume trainings
Evaluate trained agents in independent or ensemble control
Speedup training through parallelization
Focus on good Software Engineering principles: Extensibility, Agent Decoupling

Neural Network Inputs – Current Health, Weapon Cooldown, Weapon ranges (Self/Enemy), Movement Speed (Self/Enemy), Enemy in-range, Recurrent Previous Command, Distances to map edges, Enemy directional detection inputs
Neural Network Outputs – Fight/Flee, Displacement in x-axis, Displacement in y-axis
Results
The NEAT Agent successfully learnt the kiting/hit-and-run strategy for a ranged vs melee matchup in a restricted space. It learnt the optimal kiting strategy for different kind of ranged units which was robust to different starting configurations. The evolved microcontroller performed well even if the number of enemy units was increased. In addition, networks were also evolved to learn the melee-vs-ranged matchup
Results
The Sarsa Agent was applied to various complex scenarios that required creative micromanagement strategies such as kiting/hit-and-run, effective unit positioning, attack timing and evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of yourself versus the enemy. The agent successfully learnt optimal strategies for all scenarios tested.

Conclusion
Our implementations show the potential of neuroevolution and reinforcement learning for complex control problems. Through effective experimentation in StarCraft II, one can transfer the findings of this project to real-world problems such as evolving effective robotic-controllers. Our open-source NEAT-SC2 training framework along with extensive testing done with our agents represent meaningful contributions to the artificial intelligence and StarCraft II communities

Introduction:
People often relate eating alone with loneliness. A research found that eating alone may result in various health problems including depression, obesity and having metabolic syndrome. There are different constrains, like time limit and geological separation, in finding friends to gather for lunch, yet, having lunch is a good social activity to meet people. LunchToGether is a match app for lunch dates, linking people in nearby region wishing to have lunch in the same period of time together to form lunch date groups. The app features instant multiple matching. Whenever you would have lunch, launch the app, then we will make all the arrangements for you.

Our music game sets out to improve everyone's burst typing speed and stability.
Developed with Node.js, Express.js and Socket.IO, Lost Slime is a Multiplayer/Educational/Rhythm game that runs on your web browser. Written in javascript, it is designed to be lightweight and responsive to run on any machines.
Find Slimies new houses! Players in a game room compete to stack the tallest pillar to gain a high ground - which helps Slimies in spotting new locations to house. To stack a pillar block, players time their space-bars along with the music beats. But that's not it! There are phrases or sentences intertwined with, that players have to input correctly before pressing space-bar! By achieving the two objectives, Slimies can then jump on the newly stacked pillar block!
With the theme set as improving everyone's typing proficiency with music, it could be cheerful-lighthearted, or mechanically intensive. We have designed an additional beat-mapper program to translate music pieces into custom track information used by the game, in json format. METHODOLOGY
IoT Integration w/ RN App & Proximity Sensor
With N-to-1 topology owing to pub/sub pattern in MQTT, multiple applications or devices can trigger Toggle. For the project, React Native App (iOS/Android) and a IR Proximity sensor is used to trigger Toggle.
- Mobile App can either Toggle realtime or set a weekly routine for turning on/off.
- IoT IR sensor, which is also built from Toggle PCB, triggers Toggle when there is an object passed by.
It is demonstrated that the Cloud system built is highly scalable.
HTTPS Microservices on AWS
Mobile App conducts Two Factor Authorization, storing images and setting routines thanks to the microservices built on top of AWS.
AWS Lambda: Function-as-a-service
AWS DynamoDB: NoSQL Database
AWS API Gateway: HTTP API witout CORS
AWS Cognito: User Account system with authenticators
MQTTS Pub/Sub with AWS IoT (X509 Encryption)
A MQTT broker is hosted on AWS IoT Core. It is secured with TLS/SSL X509 security tokens. Unlike HTTP, MQTT is a bidirectional protocol that allows real-time update of data with very low bandwidth requirement as well as small header size, making it a more reliable IoT protocol even at places with poor connectivity.
Wi-Fi SoC Battery Saving Firmware
ESP8266 Firmware on the Toggle allows O2O monitor and control of wall switches using MQTT on AWS IoT. It has several notable functions.
1. Host Captive portal on Access Point for users to select Wi-Fi
2. Receive Flipflop Capacitive Sensor Signals
3. Drive Linear Actuator
4. MQTT Pub/Sub with X509 Security
5. Light Sleep mode that extends average battery life from 2 days to 20 days
Custom PCB w/ Wi-Fi SoC & LDO
To minimise size and weight of Toggle, custom PCB was designed and built. It is installed with ESP12S Wi-Fi SoC that has both precessor and Wi-Fi Modems. Wi-Fi SoC consumes 3.3v, whereas the Li-Po battery outputs 3.7v. To step down hte input voltage, a low dropout coltage regulator (LDO) was used. Surface mount electronic components are preferred over through hole components as it reserves more space for the opposite side of the PCB. The PCB size is 27mm*22mm*1.6mm, with HASL finish at a very minimal cost. With the right Wi-Fi SoC firmware installed on ESP12S, the PCB acts at fnul-purpose IoT platform. For instance, the IoT Proximity sensor device uses the exact same PCB as Toggle.
3D-Printed Linear Actuator
Among all the different mechanism of Linear actuators, Rack-and-Pinion with straight gears are used because:
1. Small simple shape (compared to worm gear)
2. Low electrical load (compared to Solenoid)
3. Less fatigue (compared to belt-drive)
OUTCOME
A small, low-cost and 20 days battery adhesive wall switch robot, Toggle, was built. It runs on a highly scalable AWS microservice system wtih supports to lowbandwidth MQTT protocol. Its unit manufacturing is as low as HKD$ 30.

Nowadays we often see posts of finding lost animals on social media. Also, there are posts
discussing discovering stray animals on streets. However, these social media are not
effective enough, since the news feed of users will change from time to time.

spreading information on finding lost pets and rescuing stray animals. Users can make use
of our platform to seek help. Our application will also connect to the vet clinics to make
finding vet more convenient. Our application will also update users with news focusing on
pet-caring and pet issues, these news and useful pet-caring tips will give positive influence
on users to increase their attention on animal rights.

To know more precise about the demand, the team has conducted a survey. Above is one of the results, which shows this feature is mostly considered useful.
To deal with this unsatisfied demand, we choose to facilitate an advanced query type - Spatial Pattern Matching (SPM), which is a new type of spatial group keyword query raised in recent research. Led by our supervisor, Dr. Reynold C. K. Cheng, his solutions have been well-discussed in theory. In our project, we want to fit these theories in this real-life scenario by resolving practical issues, as well as realizing some additional functionalities related to property searching. In the end, we have developed a standalone web-based application to demonstrate the importance and practicality of this newly proposed functionality.

API, algorithms and additional features
Unwanted Objects
Suppose a user who really does not like airports to be around his/her property because they are too loud, in order to specify a spatial pattern for such a request, the only way was to add the keyword 'airport' with its distance constraint set to be bigger than some very big number. However, the efficiency is suffering due to the increase of the searching range.
To deal with this problem, our team has proposed three different optimization methods and tested their performance. Users can now set a distance constraint to 'unwanted' when they are specifying their desired surroundings.

Custom Objects
Suppose some user wants to find a property that have strong ties to some specific locations, for example, his workplace or friends house. As another additional feature, we set to enable users with the ability to specify custom objects in the spatial pattern. This means that the user can add temporary objects to the PoI database with its unique keyword, which enables the user with the ability to specify the distance/directional constraints between his/her desired property and the custom object.
Directional Relations
In the SPM solutions, directional relations were not considered. However, let's suppose we have a user that wants a temple in the north of his/her property for the sake of fortune (風水), which might happen especially in HK. Therefore, we set to achieve this feature - users can now choose the direction of their desired PoIs.

Introduction:

sample series of short audio recordings that are looped back continuously. This allows users to
gradually build layers of sounds and music on their own until all the recordings combined sound
comparable to a complete band or musical piece
Currently, such technology in its physical form is very expensive (~4000HKD), hence
inaccessible to most. In light of this, LoopIt aims to make such technology accessible to the
casual user.

Supervisor: Dr. Ryan C.P. Wong
CIVL4102 Project - Tai Ho Ting Louis
The University of Hong Kong
Department of Civil Engineering
Identifying Priority Areas for the Improvement of
Minibus Service Quality
Introduction
The minibus is the third most popular form of transportation in Hong Kong, contributing 13% of all trips made in the city according to statistics provided by the Transport Department (2014). However, its popularity is still far from the more popular choices, namely rail and franchised bus which contribute 30% and 27% of all trips respectively according to the statistics. Despite that minibus is not the most important form of public transportation, it still has its significance as feeder service which connects local community to major transportation network. Therefore, this project aims to identify the priority areas for improvement of minibus services quality which could serve as a reference for related policy making in the future.
Data Collection
The primary method for data collection is an on-street questionnaire survey conducted in December 2018 in Hong Kong. 6 student research assistants are kindly recruited by the Department of Civil Engineering of the University of Hong Kong to assist data collection. This survey is conducted primarily based on simple random sampling. The student research assistants approached potential respondents face-to-face and read the questions aloud. The final sample size of the survey is 547, in which 362 are for green minibuses and 185 are for red minibuses.
10 Service Aspects Concerned
(1) Service hours
(2) Route information
(3) Waiting location
(4) Waiting time
(5) Ease of boarding
(6) Vehicle stability
(7) Safety
(8) Reliability
(9) Driver's service attitude
(10) In-vehicle comfort
Ordered Logit Model
The ordered logit model is adopted in this study to investigate the level of contribution of the 10 service aspects individually towards the overall satisfaction level. The model can be expressed in the following formulae.
Yi = 1 if Yi* ≤ k1 (1)
Yi = j if k1 ≤ Yi* ≤ kj-1 (2)
Yi = M if Yi* ≥ kM-1 (3)
Yi* = Σk=1K βkXki + εi (4)
Importance-Satisfaction Analysis
The importance-satisfaction analysis is a key part in this study which aims to identify the priority areas for improvement by studying the combined effect of importance ratings and satisfaction ratings.

Introduction:
Taking notes for books in an organized manner has always been a hard work. Not only will the
notes be lost, but they are also hard to search with. Sometimes you can't even write on a
borrowed book. BookNotes utilizes rectangular detection to allow users to scan a page of the
book and take notes on the image easily. Users can also type additional notes and add tags to
facilitate searching. Users can organise the notes according to the book they belong to by simply
scanning the barcode of the book, then the details of the books are filled in automatically.

FRing: A Geograph-based P2P Overlay Network for Fast and Robust Blockchain Systems
FYP #18006
Department of Computer Science
Faculty of Engineering
Haoran Qiu, Tao Ji
Supervised by Dr. Heming Cui
HUAWEI
SAPIENTIA ET VIRTUS
Background
Numerous blockchain systems with various consensus protocols emerges to achieve high transaction rates (2- 10K tps). However, their underlying P2P network primitives constrain further improvements due to high message redundancy and long broadcast convergence time. The first problem is caused by the excessive robustness of dominant broadcast approach Gossip. All state-of-the-art blockchain systems only tolerate 20-50% node failure while Gossip can withstand up to 90%. The reason for the second problem is that existing broadcast topologies ignore geographical distances among nodes and incur paths with unnecessarily high latency.
Introduction to FRing
We present FRING, a geography-based P2P overlay network for fast and robust broadcast in blockchain systems. FRING has three main features: sufficient robustness, low message redundancy, and fast convergence. To reduce convergence time, FRING forms the network topology by considering geographical proximity. A novel broadcast algorithm based on FRING topology is proposed to lower message redundancy while maintaining sufficient robustness. One major challenge is to eliminate the risk of topology inference by traffic pattern analysis. FRING leverages Intel SGX to guarantee nodes' behavior integrity and incorporates pattern obfuscation to prevent the traffic pattern analysis. Evaluation shows that FRING improved the throughput of EOS and HyperledgerFabric by up to 2.2X and 2.1X respectively.

Research Problems
Recent studies show that the underlying P2P network layer has become the bottleneck for transaction rate. Current blockchain systems form random P2P networks and predominantly use Gossip as the broadcast mechanism for robustness. For each hop in the broadcast process, a node pushes the message to a randomly chosen subset of its neighbors or pull from the message sender. There are two notorious problems associated with this network solution.
1. Gossip generates excessive redundant messages because Gossip is designed for extreme robustness (can tolerate up to 90% node failure). Such redundant messages lead to traffic congestion under high transaction rates.
2. Random network topology causes unnecessarily long broadcast convergence time (i.e. time used for a message to cover all nodes in the network).
Features of FRing
FRing addresses the two problems with three features:
1. Sufficient robustness: a broadcast operation can tolerate at least the same portion of node failure as the blockchain consensus protocol;
2. Low message redundancy: the messages generated in each broadcast is efficient (O(N)); and
3. Fast convergence: the convergence time are short enough so that the accumulation of old messages is reduced effectively;
FRing Topology
Conceptually, the network topology of FRING is a selfmaintained fractal ring structure, where lower level rings (typically formed by inner-region nodes) reside on higher level rings (typically formed by cross-region nodes) in a recursive way. To form this topology, FRING groups all nodes based on their geographical proximity (per-hop latency) at the bottom level. Each group forms a fully-connected ring. FRING selects multiple nodes from each ring to serve as representatives and they form a new ring in the higher level recursively. Finally, there is only one global ring remaining at the top level and all nodes are connected through representatives.

FRing Broadcast Mechanism
The broadcast mechanism of FRING is devided into three parts: broadcast up, broadcast down, and broadcast within-ring. Broadcast up and down are done with the help of representative nodes. Multiple message paths increase the robustness, which is also parametrized. Broadcast within-ring method is inspired by the distributed k-ary search method which provides O(N) message efficiency. It is done by constructing k-ary spanning trees.

ABSTRACT
Scoliosis is a medical condition where a person's spine has a sideways curve. It usually occurs before puberty and prevents the lungs from functioning properly in severe cases. Scoliosis is typically diagnosed from X-ray images, but diagnostic X-rays increase the risk of developmental problems and cancer in those exposed. This project aims to obviate children's X-ray exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis by generating X-ray images of children's backs from the corresponding harmless RGB-D images rather than capturing the X-ray images directly from the children. An RGB-D image of a back combines a standard RGB image with its depth image, and the depth image consists of the distance between each point on the back and the camera to track the spine. In this project, a deep learning model based on HRNet was built and trained to detect landmark locations of the backs on the RGB-D images first. With the detected landmarks, the X-ray images of the children's backs were eventually synthesized from the corresponding RGB-D images by another deep learning model that was built and trained based on the pix2pix model.

INTRODUCTION
This is a deep learning project that aims to synthesize X-ray images of children's backs from the corresponding RGB-D images to eliminate children's radiation exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis. This project includes three main phases, data collection, landmark detection, and X-ray synthesis. The main deliverables are two deep learning models based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis, respectively.
Implementation Details
Landmark Detection:
Input: 4-channel RGB-D images.
A Sample RGB-D Image in the Dataset.
Ground Truth & Output: six 1-channel 2D Gaussian heatmaps centered at the landmark locations.
A Sample 2D Gaussian Heatmap.
X-ray Synthesis:
Input: 10-channel RGB-D images with heatmaps centered at the predicted anatomical landmarks (after cropping and resizing).
A Sample Input in the Dataset.
Ground Truth & Output: X-ray images.
A Sample Ground Truth (left) and Output (right).
Results and Analysis
Detected Landmarks:
Analysis: our model can detect the 6 anatomical landmarks accurately on the testing dataset, and the feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Detected (right) Landmarks.
Synthetic X-ray Images:
Analysis: our model can synthesize relatively clear X-ray images with correct spine curves. The feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Synthetic (right) X-ray Images.
CONCLUSION
With the two deep learning models for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model, this project achieved its goal of generating X-ray images of children's backs from their corresponding RGB-D images with satisfactory results.

The DDCC serves as for promoting, learning and applying the use of digital technologies to enhance design, productivity, sustainability, safety and quality of the construction industry in Hong Kong.
The Digital Design & Construction Centre (DDCC) comprises Podium, North Wing, South Wing and a bridge. The buildings complex has form a 'CIC' logo from the plan view.
About the Digital Design and Construction Centre (DDCC)
Design Concept:
The Digital Design & Construction Centre (DDCC) comprises Podium, North Wing, South Wing and a bridge. The buildings complex has form a 'CIC' logo from the plan view.
Building Form:
The gardens are designed on both the ground level and roof of North Wing. It provides a large area of greenery and serves as an ideal place for leisure purpose. The site acts as a green area surrounded by highly urbanized area.
Spatial Arrangement:
The South Wing focuses on providing facilities for education purpose, while the North Wing mainly provides large open area workshops. Two wings are connected with a bridge. A restaurant is provided on the large roof garden of North Wing.
Connectivity: Underground car parks are provided to users and visitors arriving by cars. And within the building, each wing is vertically connected with a service core from the basement to the rooftop level.
Computational Design, Engineering, Analysis and Optimisation:
BIM allows visualisation of different building services systems in a building. It can help detecting clashes and avoid potential hazards. Environmental analysis has been completed for optimisation of design. For example, air flow analysis, solar radiation analysis and shadow analysis.
BIM approach:
Demonstrating a specialisation of tasks in the BIM application, we link the separated RVT files together after completion of each sub-file. It allows us to check the compatibility of building elements.
DfMA:
Building components can be easily fabricated which greatly facilitates the MiC effectively.
Sustainability:
For utilising renewable energy, wind turbines and solar panels are installed to enhance the sustainability of building. Various green features are found in the building. Greenery and vertical greening on the facade is illustrated. It helps sustainable development in environmental aspect. The glass canopy on roof allows an utilisation of natural lights.
Constructability:
BIM allows better construction management and supervision process. It greatly enhances the constructability and buildability.
Safety Planning:
The accurate location and connection of electricity services can be visualised in BIM. It allows better safety planning when carrying out indoor construction or maintenance work.
Quality of Design:
BIM facilitates the MEP design by identifying the smaller components in HVAC System. The BIM technology can visualise the whole plumbing system and facilitate overall planning.
Summary:
BIM technology can enhance the building by optimising the architectural, MEP and structural design. It improves the overall building performance efficiency and effectiveness.
