Visible text:
RoboFish
Presented by BREED HKU – bio-inspired robotics organization at the University of Hong Kong
Aim
This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.
Our current objective through this endeavor is to learn about the biomechanics of fish and other underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand how the movements are affected by different variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The model can be applied in surveillance systems and the study of marine biology.
Figure 1. Initial Design.
Hardware
RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered by a battery.
The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was designed by the mechanical team to translate the rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion. In the future, more features such as remote controlling and surveillance systems aim to be added.
Software
Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.
Current stage:
Skeleton code for the fish working.
Skeleton code for the controller.
Background research on simulators.
Next stage:
Incorporating a simulator to simulate the environment of the swimming pool (the trial test environment for the model).
Through simulation, variation of different parameters of the fish to analyze which conditions provide best speed and energy efficiency.
Design
The goal is an ideal fish model mechanically designed to possess the following characteristics:
Streamlined body.
Minimum drag, especially at the edges and in the gaps between separate components.
Low weight.
Floating stability and buoyancy.

Conclusion and Applications
We believe that there are several applications of our project for research in the academic world. Our model can be used to analyze marine biology through exploration of the sea. A significant possibility is thus the application of surveillance systems, not just in ecosystems research, but also in the navy.

The Automatic Chair Parking System aims to provide a smart solution in classroom and other similar environment by helping to move and arrange chairs, while reducing the risk of occupational injuries and potential dangers related to the repetitive works. Game Design
Hexplore Fort is a single-player RPG AR Android Mobile Game that highly referenced to the clssic game [Tower of the Sorcerer). Player are in a role of villain, and they are required to control the spider-like robot (Hexapod) to explore the virtual fort augmented by AR in order to capture the princess.
Map Generation by Plane Detection
Plane detection in ARCore is enabled to look for clusters of feature points for environmental understanding, so that the game can create an anchor point on the detected horizontal flat surface when the players click on the screen. ARCore tracks the position of the anchor over time, the map will seems to be fixed on the floor as a result.
Robot Recognition by Image Tracking
Image recognition is enabled to track the referenced images pre-built in the database, so that the game can recognize the image stuck on the body of hexapod. The 3D eyes model of the hexapod will be augmented onto the robot for interacting with the virtual augmented terrain.
Hexapod Connection and Control
Classic Bluetooth with SPP is used to establish the connection between the mobile phone and the Arduino-based Hexapod. Formatted Bluetooth commands are sent out for movement control at a regular time interval of 0.2 seconds to balance the time given to hexapod for response and the number of commands missed.
Movements like walking, picking up items, actions for celebration and different kinds of fighting actions are used in the game.

Raw Data - The calculation procedures rely on two raw data sources from MTR: SICP logs and timetables. SICP logs provide information about actual train movements, while timetables provide information about scheduled train movements. During the development process, both data sources should be provided in the form of batches of historical data. In the production environment, SICP logs should be provided to the system in real time, while timetables only need to be updated when there are changes.
Preprocessing - Raw data obtained are preprocessed to extract the relevant data. For SICP logs, Relevant lines (TKNU and TKOC) in KTL are extracted. Relevant data (actual arrival time, station, track, and train) are then extracted from the TKNU records. Actual departure time is then determined by finding the nearest TKOC-2 records happening afterwards in the same track. Platform tracks, where trains stop during their dwell time in a station, are identified in the stop column, according to the list of tracks extracted manually from the track diagram. Hourly data is then combined into daily data. Timetables are parsed by replacing destination codes (e.g. 114) with stations. Due to the limitation of MTR's timetable system, the effective timetable for one day is split into two timetables. Hence, the timetables are merged according to internal rules.
Matching - Matching phase is the core of the delay calculation procedures, which locates the actual trip a train is serving based on actual arrival time in the SICP logs and scheduled arrival timed in the timetables. Delays are then calculated simply by their difference.
In a normal day without incidents, the actual trip a train is serving is located by matching actual arrival time in SICP logs of platform tracks to the nearest scheduled arrival time in the timetable, with the same train and station. This method minimises the arrival delay of trains, which is consistent with the goal of train scheduling. The arrival and departure delays (in seconds) can then be calculated as differences between actual and scheduled time. However, there are some train movements that are not serving a trip, and hence should not be associated with the timetable. Therefore, when one timetable entry is matched to two SICP logs, only the one with the smallest absolute arrival delay will be kept. Besides, during the development process, outliers in the training data are removed based on z-score. Z-scores are calculated on arrival delays, and SICP logs with z-score higher than 3 are detected as outliers.
The matching procedures in a day with incidents are the same as those in the normal case, which can handle different types of incidents seamlessly. In case of train changeover, the replacement train carries the same train number, and the SICP logs associated to the timetable are expected to be the same as the normal case, due to the principle of minimization of arrival delay. In case of train withdrawal, train cancellation, or trip cancellation, as the timetable remains unchanged, the matching procedures will assign trains to timetables based on the principle of minimization of arrival delay, which is aligned to the behaviour of train operators.
Simulation Model
To simulate train operations, running times and dwelling times derived from datasets are used to calibrate and validate the model. The ultimate goal of the development of the model is to reproduce the behaviour pattern of the railway system in the past, and predict the effect of different types of events on the operations. While some related works calculate running times and dwell times using train movement equations and traffic conditions, a data-driven approach is adopted in this project, since a large amount of track occupancy data is provided by MTR. Regression-based models and bayesian networks are tried in our experiments to predict arrival delays. The regression approach captures the distribution of running times and dwell times due to external conditions without manual tuning of parameters, and does not require the knowledge of train motion characteristics. It is also more adaptive for future changes in timetables and extensions to other lines. Bayesian network is a type of statistical model which represents the conditional dependencies of a group of variables in the form of a directed acyclic graph. A dynamic Bayesian network in particular can be utilized for time series prediction for the train, using the day and time as explanatory variables, since certain times during particular days may tend to be more crowded than others.

Data Analysis
Train Movement Analysis
Journey Delay Analysis
Timetable Analysis
Passenger Flow Analysis
Train movements are time-dependent, as train delays in different periods of a day vary significantly, which is likely to be affected by different train schedules and fluctuations in passenger demands. This finding supports the conclusion that time and location are two key factors in designing the simulation model.
Two months of train operation logs are obtained for data analysis. In order to divide the logs into normal days (no incidents observed) and abnormal days (minor or major incidents observed), the journey delay is extracted from individual train operations. Journey delay is defined as the arrival delay at the destination, which is the last station of a train trip. The destination is determined by the train number according to an internal naming rule used by MTR. In normal days, two peaks of delays can be observed during two periods (8 AM - 9 AM, 6 PM - 7 PM), which corresponds to two peak hours by commuters, confirmed by the passenger inflow and outflow analysis. In general, the distribution of journey delays cluster around zero. In abnormal days, while there are major incidents with substantial delays, most of the incidents are minor and only affect the train service briefly.
The arrival delay distribution in different stations generally approximates normal distribution, with notable exceptions of some busy stations, such as KWT (Kwun Tong). For the busy stations, there are two peaks observed around zero and positive delay, indicating frequent occurrences of noticeable delays. One of the terminal stations, TIK (Tiu Keng Leng) is also distinct with its peak of negative delay, which shows that the design of timetable leaves extra buffers for the actual train operations. The medians of arrival delays among different stations generally stay around zero in normal days, which shows that the timetable design is reasonable and reflects the actual train operations well. However, TRK is still the noticeable exception, as mentioned previously.
The MTR provided a passenger flow dataset. The dataset is split into two files: one for inflow and one for outflow. Both files contain data aggregated at 1 minute intervals for all the 96 stations. We carried out extensive exploratory data analysis, during which the correlations between inflow and outflow across various stations was analysed. Several interesting correlations were discovered such as between inflow at KOT and outflow at WTS. Conversely uncorrelated stations have also been discovered.

As the objective of the project is to minimise the delays suffered by the train, the potential benefits from the impact of this project include, but are not limited to, a reduction in delays, improved efficiency and time management, lower probability of the MTR being penalised by the government for extensive delays and time being saved for commuters. Should the project be successful in implementing a simulation model and recommendation system, it may possibly pave the way for driverless trains in the future, as the current MTR trains are operated by train operators.

Background
Usually, if we would like to measure something at home, there can be some very large professional device, or we can use some small liquid level meter (also known as gradienter). However, such kind of level meter is not ideal - the precision can be low as you are reading where the bubble is.
Other approaches, like a digital level meter, which can display exact values of the gradient degrees, is not desirable enough due to its high price and difficult operations. So for this project, I am thinking if we can make a digital level meter and something more inside SenseHat to use it, make it intuitive and particularly when we DIY something at home.
SeneHat is a fascinating piece of hardware. It has all kinds of sensors, and an IMU included. Through reading IMU and other sensors' readings, we can show intuitively on the the screen of SenseHat the result we are measuring.
Low precision
[unreadable]
More on IMU
IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), among many others, and spacecraft, including satellites and landers. [1]
An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear acceleration using one or more accelerometers and rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a heading reference. Typical configurations contain one accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each of the three vehicle axes: pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat uses a library called RTIMULib to implement the interface for reading from its IMU.
Function Implementations
Func 1: Digital Level Meter
This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch and roll values from the board. When the program detects that roll is bigger than 45 or smaller than -45 degrees, the program will switch to pitch measure mode. In this mode, a line will be displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally. When roll is between -45° and 45°, the program will switch to pitch and roll measure mode. There will be two circles displayed on SenseHat, and they will become closer if pitch and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.
To draw lines programmatically on SenseHat, I have also written a library called sensehat_graphic. The implementation graph looks as follows:

SenseHat comes with a compass, so we can know which direction is North or South by setting two small dots on the border of the screen. We can also know how many degrees we have turned. By reading the change of yaw value, we can visualise it on the display. This is also similar to the feature in compass app in iOS. MECH4429 Integrated Capstone Experience
Design, Build and Fly
Summary
With the ever-growing demand for air cargo capacity comes the pursuit for cargo aircraft that combine a large payload with optimum efficiency. The Design, Build and Fly (DBF) team set out to meet this challenge by creating a radio-controlled model airplane, to compete in the Payload Challenge organized by the British Model Flying Association (BMFA). The process involved careful research into aeronautical engineering theories and creative solutions. The effectiveness of the design was proved in test flights by two fully functional prototypes. Various issues were identified during the trials, carefully examined, and subsequently addressed in an iterative manner. The team has continuously implemented modifications to the design, in an effort to produce the model plane that would carry the target payload with the highest efficiency attainable, and the results will hopefully provide useful insights for future model builders and aircraft engineers alike.
Competition Rules
The competition, "Challenge 4 – Quantity" of the BMFA Payload Challenge, requires all participating teams to design, construct, and fly an "electric powered, radio controlled aircraft", to "transport the greatest number of 150 +/- 10mm diameter polystyrene spheres of mass 35 +/- 5g (see Figure 1) around a predetermined course (Figure 2) in the three 6-minute time slots utilising a standardised propulsion unit [1].

Design and Construction
To verify the design concept, the first prototype was designed on a 1:2 scale.
Feedback collected from the first flight test contributed to the modification of the design, leading to a full-scale second prototype fully compliant with the competition requirements.
The design process relied on the use of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software (Figure 3).
Finite Element Analysis (FEA) was carried out on individual parts to predict their behaviour under loading (Figure 4).
To ensure a high level of precision, construction rigs (Figure 5) and laser-engraved templates (Figure 6) were used.
Figure 3 CAD model of the 2nd prototype
Figure 4 FEA performed on the motor mount
Figure 5 Construction rigs used in building the wings
Figure 6 Templates used in the the construction of the vertical stabilizer
Technical Specifications and Performance
Two flight tests were carried out on 19 Feb 2020 (1st prototype) and 23 March (2nd prototype) at Hong Kong Model Engineering Club's (HKMEC) model plane airport in Yuen Long, Hong Kong.
The first prototype crashed immediately after take-off during the first trial. After improvisatory modifications were made on site, the test was able to continue.
The first prototype completed two successful flight cycles, justifying the feasibility of the design.
Figure 7 Both prototypes parked alongside each other
Issues identified were fed into the design of the second prototype. Major improvements included a more streamlined fuselage, larger wings, strengthened landing gear, adjusted motor placement and improved tail shape.
While some issues persisted and new problems were identified, the second prototype was overall a success and ready to be used in the competition.

Conclusions
During the 10 months between July 2019 and April 2020, the team successfully designed, constructed, and flew two prototypes. The final product satisfied most of our initial design objectives. The team first conducted in-depth research into flight theories and aircraft design principles, before designing and modifying the plane through an iterative process. Despite the cancellation of the competition, our project remains valuable as it will offer insights into the aircraft design process for future engineers from the model building community as well as from the industry.

Competition & Goals
Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJI during the summer vacation on a yearly basis. It combines technology and e-gaming competition style, thus being exciting and unconventional.
The path to victory consists of the following steps:
Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and restrictions
Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A 0HP enemy base is a victory for your team.
HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017. We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical experience gained during the preparation and participation process. Our work is divided into technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm development.
Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield
Mechanical & Hardware designs
The mechanical and hardware design of each robot is based on detailed planning. For each of the robot, we prepared the following technical files before turning concepts into reality:
Requirement list
Mechanical layout & actuation plan
Hardware schematic
The following are the examples of our design. They are:
Standard (top left): an agile robot on the ground that delivers moderate firepower and smart detection features
Sentry (top right): a fully auto robot running on a rail near the base. Its firepower is for defense
Hero (bottom left): A heavy robot dealing the most damage with special projectiles
Engineer (bottom right): A utility robot that fires, rescues slain robots and delivers special projectiles to the Hero robot
Figure 2. The designs of robots
Technical Management
Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of development. It should also regulate the development so that it proceeds in a more orderly way.
The efforts we made this season include:
Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical and methodology knowledge.
Archive system, which governs the naming and organization of development files
Documentation system, which specifies the technical details that can be referred to during development to minimize confusion.
Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design. These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance solidarity.
Algorithm development
To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with computer vision are also favorable.
For software and algorithm design, we also come up with detailed plans before development. The plan is known as software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carrier out for fine-tuning.

Introduction
Studies on configurations of drones with high energy efficiency in have been emerging. However, few canard configuration drones were designed, despite its great potential in minimizing weight. The Design, Build, Fly (DBF) project is a circumstances to design a canard configuration airplane and prove the concept design. Through this project, not only could students understand and apply relevant aeronautical knowledge and design and manufactures skills, students could tangibly experience the whole engineering design process as a team. Ultimately, our goal is to participate in the annual BMFA Payload Challenge 2020 held in Buckminster, UK.

BMFA
The British Model Flying Association (BMFA) is the United Kingdom's National Governing Body for the sport of model aircraft flying and one of its key aims is to increase interest in aviation and engineering through education.
The BMFA Payload Challenges require students to design, build and fly load-carrying model aircraft. The competitions have evolved to stretch the abilities of participating students and there is no doubt the development of a good aircraft requires each team to display design flair, technical knowledge and teamwork.
Canard Airplanes
Unlike conventional aircrafts with a tail, canard airplanes benefit from weight reduction due to reduction in overall length of the airplane and reduction in Lift force required. However, canard airplanes are sensitive to Location of Centre of Gravity, as a wrong location could result in an unstable airplane. To produce a stable design, sophisticated computer simulations were used to achieve the optimum wing configurations and location of Centre of Gravity.

Introduction>
Our team develops a novel reusable face mask using electrospun nanofibers based filter material. It is expected to partially solve the technical, social and environmental problems related to the current one-time using face masks.
Technique>
Electrospinning is a matured technique to fabricate nanofibers (e.g., dimension at nm level) which are much smaller than the melt-blown fibers (e.g., dimension at μm level) used in the current face masks. The nanofibrous filter has a high porosity (e.g., > 80%) to allow air filtration with low resistance, meanwhile its large internal surface area enable the great capacity for air pollutants capture. In addition, the electrospinning technique is very flexible to coordinate with other physicochemical approaches to improve the structure and chemistry of the nanofibrous filters for highly efficient air filtration.

Pacifî
Pacifî is a mobile application for iOS and Andriod, which aims to Relax the User, Recharge their mind and allow them to Relect on their actions and thoughts. All of this allows for sustainable healthy mind.
This is achieved through the Emotion Wheel and the four activities used to destress.
Emotion Wheel is a medium for reflecting the results of sentimental analysis and other activities. Emotion Wheel uses computer vision as well activity-specific Algorithms to understand feelings of the user. The Wheel visualises the user's emotion which leads to interpretation which allows the user to understand reasons of their stress better and work on them for the future.
JOG
Jog is allows user to listen to their favourite music while trotting reduces stress hormones in body. It also sends more nourishing blood to the brain which helps user think more clearly. Stepcount is shown to create a sense of achievement.
BREATHE
Breathe uses 4 second respiration technique as a way to adjust emotion to more relaxing state. As an injunctive therapy, it should be used in conjunction with other activities.
BUDDY
Buddy is smart bot that uses socratic questioning, facial analyses along with natural language processing to help user complain and understand their emotions. Not only talking allows the user to get destress as it gets it out of their system but also helps user express their emotion anonymously without feeling judged The machine learning agent (bot) was trained using special user survey created by the team.
DOODLE
Doodle relieves psychological distress by expressing emotions. It can also help in memory retention, which can be useful during reflection.

OUR PROJECT AIM
This project aims to design and build a fabric roll edge extractor to replace the practice of labor operation in this procedure. The fabric roll edge extractor will extract an adhesive tape from a roll of fabric within 1 minute in an all-dry process. Full automation processes can be replaced with the actual model in the current human production line thus reducing operation cost and human errors with higher efficiency.
OUR PROJECT SOLUTION
The device was divided into four mechanical processes including tape locating, loosening, removing, and disposal, respectively. After an array of research and analysis, we decided to use a diffuse sensor for tape sensing, heat guns for tape loosening, hook for tape removing, and pressurized air gun for disposal.
FUTURE IMPROVEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
1. Vertical axis actuation of the extractor
2. Replacement of the sensor
3. Integrate the location of fabric edge with NFC module
4. Tape disposal with pressurized air nozzle
5. Setup a database for different fabric materials
CONCLUSION
Different tests are conducted to ensure the evaluation criteria can be met as this is the crucial requirement from our client, Fong's National Engineering Co. Ltd. The testing results showed all requirements are met. From the perspective of functionality and feasibility in the test, this prototype meets the passing standard and can be built into an actual model for the automation of the fabric roll edge extraction process.

SMART MASK
Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, a face mask has help us to reduce the spread of the COVID-19 viruses. The use of the mask has been substantially increased. For further enhancing the functionality of the mask, it is desirable for developing a smart product with an integration of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, mobile devices, and cloud computing. The smart product has the following features to minimize the spread of the COVID-19:
· Monitor and record the air quality of the surrounding;
· Notify users if the surrounding air quality is not acceptable;
· Keep track of the user's geolocations for facilitating an easy identification of suspected users;
· Publish the potentially hazardous areas to the users after analytics of collected data;
· Can be used for many times with an appropriate replaceable filter; and
· Reduce environmental pollution.
As a result, the proposed smart mask would help building a safe and green community.
SMART DESIGN
The smart mask is washable and reusable for multiple times. Only the replacement of the air filters is required to maintain the best functionality of the air purification. A sensor for measuring the air quality is equipped in the smart mask. Therefore, the user can be notified whenever the quality of air falls below the standard by using a cloud-based platform and a mobile app and thus avoid staying in an environment with stale air. Moreover, the smart mask can be used as a normal mask by removing the sensor part.
WHY IS IT BETTER THAN A REGULAR MASK?
In the past few months, mask waste has been increased, which has resulted in the increase of plastic pollution. However, one of the characteristics of the smart mask is that it can be reused multiple times. They can be washed by water and used for several months. After a few times of use, only the air filters need to be replaced for consistent clean air; but it still contributes tremendously to the environment.

Self-healing, microencapsulation and granular materials
Department of Civil Engineering ,University of Hong Kong
Name: Chow Cheuk Hei Scott
Supervisor : Dr. Sérgio D.N. Lourenço
INTRODUCTION
Foundation quality is of paramount importance to all civil engineering works. Since it governs the safety of the structures and buildings stood above it. However, settlement in foundation is found very common, in which it comes as a natural deterioration process. Maintenance work for foundation can be challenging and costly. Having said that, inspired by the adopting of self-healing capsules in concrete improvement, this study aims to mimic and incorporate similar self-healing technology in strengthening of soil.
METHODOLOGY
The main goal of this study is to examine whether self-healing materials can be encapsulated and added to the soil to improve its strength. Other objectives include the effect of pH and temperature on capsules formation through complex coacervation and the self-healing effects of microcapsules under different load application and healing time. Complex Coacervation is proposed as the method to produce microcapsules, while shear box test will be the core methodology used in assessing the self-healing ability of microcapsules when added into soil for improvement. It is hoped this study could promote the use of self-healing microcapsules as a mean for soil improvement in the engineering industry, thereby reducing the cost for maintenance of foundation and also improving the durability and safety of the structures.
SELF HEALING MECHANISM

Capsule based self-healing, as its name suggest, the capsule is made to provide mechanical protection to the healing agent. When cracks occur, the shell of the capsule will be ruptured. As a result, the core materials inside the capsule will leak out and then undergo some chemical reactions and produce substances, which acts as glue to seal the crack together, achieving the self-healing behaviour.
COMPLEX COACERVATION
a process in which two oppositely charged wall materials react to form the capsule of the core material. Gelatin and Gum Arabic are commonly used as the capsule materials. Gelatin is a protein, while Gum Arabic is a polysaccharide.

RESULTS
The preliminary results show that capsules can be produced through complex coacervation and it has displayed some signs of self-healing effects exerted on the sand sample. Further testing will be conducted to justify the self-healing ability of the microcapsules. In the future, one will investigate the self-healing effects of the capsules under different parameters such as applied load, microcapsule content as well as healing time.

1. Motivation
Figure 1: Spookiness of quantum mechanics: reversing one of the two zero capacity quantum channels enables us to send information.
Conventionally, information suffers from exponential decay in long distance transmission. However, in exciting projects like building the quantum internet, an information carrier has to pass through many intermediate quantum servers before reaching the receiver. Such a goal cannot be achieved without a scheme of reliably transmitting data over a long sequence of noisy channels. Chiribella et al.[1] formulated the second level of quantization of quantum information theory by considering the superposition of quantum trajectories and quantum channels and demonstrated communication advantage of this model. One then asks can it provide any hope in the formidable task of preserving information?
2. Our results
We answer the above question on the positive end. Perhaps astonishingly, asymptotically a sequence of asymptotically many superposed pure quantum erasure channels preserves quantum information with the facilitation of Kraus operators. Overall, our results:

IMSE2121 - Engineering Training
SMART
AGV
SMART PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT
Automated Guided Vehicle
What is Our Product?
Our product is a smart miniaturized Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) with a body design of the iconic Hong Kong trams. Our mini AGV could move along a guided path and make its own decisions (turn left, right, or stop) autonomously. There is a open compartment on the rear upper level of our AGV, which could be useful to better visualize actual-sized AGV. Furthermore, our AGV has an Arduino-based controller, which could be easily programmed by the mBlock software.
Objective and Target Audience
Our objective is to create a STEM-oriented product that could increase students' interests in the world of robotics, logistics, and automation This product is targeted towards Primary and Secondary school educators who need a more fun and approachable way to introduce this technology to the newer generation. By combining the design of Hong Kong trams, the cultural icon of Hong Kong itself, with this smart AGV, students would be more attracted and interested to learn more about AGVs and robotics in general.
Design and Manufacturing of Smart AGV
1.Design Planning and Sketching
2.CAD Modelling using SOLIDWORKS
3. Parts Manufacturing
a. 3D Printing for the main body
b. Laser Cutting for Acrylic-based part
c. Water Jet Cutting for Metal-based part
4. Full Asssembly of all parts
FUN FACT:
This is our first hand-drawn sketch of the AGV!
[unreadable]
Smart Design Feature
Snap-Fit Joints between the Bodies
The snap-fit connections for the main frame/chassis of the bot was adopted to prevent the addition of unnecessary screw holes and made the AGV much lighter and much less complicated. This feature also allows the internal parts of the bot could be easily inspected.
Smart Sensors and Control
Arduino-based Main Control Board
We have incorporated our code into the arduino-based board which is the brains and nerves of this AGV and this is what gives it its distinct, adaptive, flexible and scalable characteristics and functionality. The arduino board is very responsive and can be updated in real time making the software to hardware transfer and integration very effective and smooth.
Ultrasonic Sensor
[unreadable]
This component records distance data specified from the bot to the nearest object. Advanced versions of these sensors can be implemented in driverless cars and also in factory equipment such as conveyor belts as a future and more industry specific use.
Line Follower
This component uses light sensors to monitor the location of the bot on a given line and update it to the motors in real-time in case some changes to the path need to be made. These can be and are already being used in a much more comprehensive and complex way in the manufacturing and future development of the automotive industry.
Future Design Development
New Other AGV Design
Creating other attractive and iconic designs would increase the students interests toward the product
Additional Sensor
Installing additional sensor, such as Light or Sound sensors, could increase the complexities and accuracy of the AGV during a task. This is of course would create more challenges for the students!
Additional Part
Adding more complex parts, such as an elevated/moving compartment would also increase the difficulties and skills of the AGV

Introduction
Abnormal embryonic development leads to severe birth defects and diseases such as dysmelia. Recent studies have shown that the embryo of Caenorhabditis elegans (C.elegans), a model organism, undergoes abnormal elongation when cellular anisotropy and plasticity cannot be developed and maintained properly. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

Novelty of the project
To understand the physical origin of abnormal embryo elongation, we developed a dynamic model (within the framework of continuum mechanics and thermodynamics) to
(1) elucidate how cellular anisotropy and plasticity are gradually developed in the embryo wall during its elongation;
(2) show how the elongation process is sustained and stabilized by the development of anisotropy and plasticity in cells;
(3) reveal that insufficient myosin activity and excessive severing of F-actin bundles are two major causes for abnormal embryo elongation.

generation

ONCE THE WORLD'S FASTEST ROBOTIC FISH --
NOW READY TO DOMINATE THE SEA.
Objectives
Enhance manoeuvrability to navigate through real-world terrains
Improve waterproofing technique for continuous deployment in water bodies
Increase robustness and efficiency of mechanical/electrical system
Increase controllability by providing better user experience
Swimming across the harbour from Central to TST, our robotic fish will prove its applicability in seawater.
Along with its previous speed record and additional features, it can be beneficial to our society. For instance, its biomimetic nature doesn't interfere with marine life like other underwater vehicles with turbines.
Not only is the new model much more energy efficient, less polluting, but it is also environmentally friendly as it is constructed with less material.
Limitless Underwater Motion Control
The robot consists of 3 main control protocols: the Roll, Pitch and Yaw.
We have developed full motion control of the robotic fish with the aid of Motor Feedback system and PID control of the high-torque servo motor. A DIY controller with simply input from joysticks and a potentiometer is developed to provide accurate and quick control of the robot. With the aid of a suitable configuration for our RC set-up, we have achieve a range of 10m for communication.
Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
Mimicking a fish-like streamlined shape, the drag from the surrounding water current is reduced.
With a new, specialized design, we are able to achieve 100% waterproofing with 3D printing only.
The reinforcement with stainless steel rods has given us sufficient rigidity to overcome the oscillation produced by high-speed travelling.
The complex bearing system at the tail section has ensured a smooth motion with a very low energy loss.
From the previous testing, our chassis is certified to be completely waterproofed for at least 24 hours, while also being able to support the fish for a service time of at least 2 months.

Introduction
The world's fastest swimming robotic fish: a robot that aims to mimic the propulsive behavior of real biological fishes, designed to swim in the complex dynamics of open waters. Our fish swims at low frequency of 4 Hz, a cruising speed of 2m/s with an input power of 150W, and can achieve high acceleration with a compact and compliant tail-like propulsor.
Fig 1. The robotic fish – latest design.
Remote Control Implementation
The controls are implemented through the Raspberry Pi and Arduino, where the Arduino is used mainly for GPIO to send data to the Pi.
A custom-built controller was designed using the APC 220 433MHz RF receiver & transmitters (available with the Arduino).
A custom communication mechanism sends power signals and turning signals to the fish. An auto timer is also implemented to prevent the controller from overflowing the buffer of the receiver.
The orientation of the fish and fins is controlled using input from motion and orientation data, which is achieved with an inertial measurement unit (IMU).
The Pi utilizes its fast CPU to process the data, controlling servos with input from the camera while running machine learning (ML) models.
With the Sense HAT board, the Pi provides an accelerometer and gyro which maintain the orientation of the fish by a negative feedback loop and servo (fins) control.
Upcoming soon, we plan to perform system integration to connect the control systems and sensors of the robot with computer vision components.
We also aim to work towards deep reinforcement learning (Deep RL) for obstacle navigation.
Fig 5. INU for motion control.
Design & Manufacture
The latest version consists of about 250 individual components assembled together. The dimensions are 1250mm x 150mm x 520mm with a mass of 13 kg. The parts were 3D-modelled on SolidWorks, where simulations were run to test the performance of the fish body. A scaled-down version was 3D printed or CNC machined for proof-of-concept.
The materials used to manufacture the robot are PLA plus plastic, aluminium, rubber, and acrylic. Various manufacturing methods have been used including 3D printing, CNC machining, and traditional hand tooling methods such as cutting, drilling, sanding, soldering, etc. The electrical and electronic components such as the motor, encoder, batteries, Arduino, Raspberry Pi and the wirings are sealed in acrylic tubes.
Several versions of the robotic fish were built. Each body differed in size and aerodynamic properties, with tails varying in shape, size, and material to try to achieve the best performance.

Factors Affecting Performance
The relation between body length and fish swimming speed:
For a motor with given power and the same tail design, an increase in length of the fish was found to cause less vibration during motion. This is because as length increased, the buoyancy, mass and inertia increased as well. Hence, newer versions of the fish were built with a longer body to improve speed.
The influence of tail design and amplitude on fish swimming speed:
It was found that with a solid tail cannot make the best of the motor. With the motor working against the rigid tail, speed was reduced. To solve this, a flexible 3D-printed tail was built. The new tail can bend and can absorb energy, significantly reducing the load on the motor. The size of the tail was also increased, as a bigger tail area allows it to push more water. However, a size that is too large would increase the load on the motor and ultimately burn it. Similarly, if the amplitude of tail movement is too low, speed is low, but if amplitude is too high, it increases load. After testing several different tails and amplitudes, an optimal design was finally achieved.

Use Cases
Surveillance and Data Gathering
Unregulated fishing practices have reduced fishery resources in local waters. As a surveillance device intended for data collection and marine research, our fish can be used to monitor illegal fishing.
Top-notch surveillance using computer vision technology can be used to look for illegal fishers and detect entangled fish in broken fishing nets.
Plastic Collection
We aim to use this technology to tackle marine litter and water pollution, a serious issue with huge environmental impact.
Computer vision can be geared towards the detection of plastics, with a garbage collector added to the fish to gather litter.
Oil Spills
Oil spills may take weeks or years to clean up. Using a swarm of "oil sharks", this could be possible in just a few days, minimizing severe environmental effects.
The technologies of UV fluorescence analyzer or non-dispersive/fixed filter IR analyzer can be adapted to the fish for oil detection in water.
Aquaculture
To improve fishing and aquaculture processes, the robotic fish can use its speed and vision technology to survey the bottom of trawling nets
The fish can also serve as an ultrasonic bot to assist in the clean-up of biofouling (harmful buildup on fish nets).
Achievements
THE VAYU PROJECT
1. Guinness World Record holder for "The fastest 50m swim by a robotic fish".
2. "Caudal-Fin based Turning Mechanism for an Underactuated Fast Swimming Robotic Fish" published at the International Conference for Marine Robotics 2019 held on September 17-19, 2019, at St. Petersburg State Marine Technical University, Russia.
3. "Development of High Performance Mechanical Robotic Fish" published in the 8th PAAMES meeting and AMEC held on October 9-12, 2018, in Busan, South Korea.

Problem

Solution
Matchbox is an open-source
hardware project where we
design DIY controller kits
from recycled keyboards
and common components.
Features
Passion
Engage and educate children with
subject matter that they are most
passionate about - games!
Projects
Kit is designed to be an accessible
entryway into hardware and electronics
with much expansion potential for the
kids to discover on their own.
Peers
Supports up to 4 players! Encourages
students to collaborate and complete
the kit together.
Play
The controller is a staple of play. With
this kit the kids will not only learn about
electronics while putting it together,
they will also end up with an awesome
controller to play their creations with!
Accessible
Since the keyboard component is
recycled, we can reduce the cost and
provide more students with the unique
opportunity to start learning STEM.
Next steps
Custom PCB prototype,
testing our first batch of
prototypes with kids,
refining, and more
testing...

and bringing this into
real classrooms!

Home to the Fire Dragon Dance as well as the site for Hong Kong's first dairy farm
Student Interest Group (SIG) - Engineering and Archaeology is organizing a fieldtrip to Pokfulam Village, a local historical site in the west of Hong Kong Island.
In this trip, you will learn about the tradition of the Fire Dragon Dance and see how the dragons are hand-crafted. You will visit the remains of the former dairy farm, hear the villagers' stories about growing up in this village and their memories of the farm which used to provide Hong Kong with fresh milk and offer employment to the villagers. You can also try out an Augmented Reality (AR) app to reconstruct the remains of the former dairy farm.
Join us to study how the villagers are striving to restore and reuse the historic houses facing pressure from urban redevelopment plans, explore the sustainable ways to conserve and manage the village, and think about how you can contribute your technical and engineering skills to studying and preserving the past!

Innovative ways to automate archaeological work?
Did you know there was an ancient pottery-making industry in HK? Do you want to uncover the secrets of how families joined together to use local resources to make ceramics? Join us on an archaeological field trip to follow the clues of past human activity through the Tai Po River valley. Learn about the historic Wun Yiu temple, trek through banana fields and jungle to discover hidden artifacts of the past, see how animals were used to grind materials, explore deep into a cave rich in porcelain minerails... We will take you on a trip to the centuries-old Win Yiu village to explore why almost half a million porcelain bowls were shipped from here across south Asia. Learn what archaeologists do, and see if you can contribute to studying the objects of the past. Archaeology is a field that has a low level of automation but needs more. During the trip, we will also think about how engineering can help archaeological fieldwork, such as through innovative ways to record and present archaeological sites and artefacts with new technologies. We will even play with an AR/VR app at the site. Let the adventure begin!

Background
There is a lack of hands-on quantum technology educational tools used in STEM education currently. We offer a compact fully-functional Quantum Demonstration Kit (QDK) to bridge this gap.

We aim to develop a teaching-oriented designing their own experimental protocols, portable setup that allows students to acquire fundamental concepts of quantum mechanics. The students can easily gain an intuitive feeling for quantum physics by

PROJECT INNOBOT
MULTI-TERRAIN QUADRAPED
Innowing Robotics Intern Team
Soogon Kim, Anson XU Shiyang
Background
Quadraped robots offer several advantages for multi-terrain traversal due to their high stability, ability to negotiate uneven surfaces, and potential for redundancy in leg movements. Multi-terrain hexapods have diverse applications. They can be used in search and rescue operations, exploration of challenging environments, surveillance tasks, agricultural applications, and even entertainment or educational purposes.
Modular Robot structure
Extended legs are beneficial for climbing stairs, and a square-shaped plate enhances balance during walking. Multiple-layered structures facilitate inserting different sensors on the robot.
Inverse Kinematics algorithem for bio-inspired gait
Quadruped Inverse Kinematics (IK) is essential for enabling four-legged robots to move realistically and efficiently. These algorithms determine the joint configurations needed to position the robot's feet accurately, maintaining dynamic stability across various terrains. By mimicking natural animal gaits, IK improves the robot's ability to navigate obstacles and interact effectively with its environment.
Capability of stair climbing
The Spider Robot, inspired by spider biomechanics, adeptly navigates stairs using articulated legs for enhanced stability and flexibility. Equipped with advanced motion control algorithms, it could potentially handle complex terrains, making it ideal for search and rescue, industrial maintenance, and surveillance in inaccessible areas.

Our rover is developed from scratch with a combined system of ESP32 and Jetson Nano. It contains DC motors with encoders, and a power system for stable operation of the robot.
SLAM System for Mapping
We create a Simultaneous localization and mapping system (SLAM) for the rover to understand the new environment by map generation, and to localize itself in the scene during navigation.
Navigation (Developing)
We are developing a navigation algorithm for the rover to design an optimized path to reach the destination. The algorithm will also collect live data from LiDAR and update the path according to obstacles detected.

We Are Creating a Printing System Suitable For All
Ergonomic Integrated Management System for 3D Printers
A Project Of:
NestSpace
Makerspace Innovations
Supervisor: Dr. Ray Y. Zhong
The objective of our project is to develop a user-friendly interface for controlling a 3D printer using natural language commands. By enabling voice and keyboard input, we aim to simplify the control process for users. Our goal is to enhance accessibility and ease of use, eliminating the need for complex manual settings.
Our approach involves leveraging the power of a language model, specifically the LLM (Large Language Model), to interpret and understand verbal commands. We tuned the LLM on a dataset of 3D printing-related instructions and implemented a robust natural language processing system to accurately recognize and execute user commands, ensuring seamless interaction with the 3D printer.
Through rigorous testing and evaluation, we achieved impressive results with our LLM-powered chat-based UI for the 3D printer. The system accurately interpreted and executed a wide range of voice and keyboard commands, demonstrating its reliability and responsiveness. Users experienced a streamlined and intuitive control experience, enhancing their overall satisfaction and productivity.
Our project's successful implementation of a chat-based UI powered by LLM for 3D printers has significant implications. It revolutionizes the way users interact with 3D printers, simplifying the control process and making it accessible to a wider audience. This innovation has the potential to boost productivity, reduce user errors, and encourage further advancements in human-machine interaction within the 3D printing industry.

ARMSTRONG
ROBOTIC ARM DIGITAL TWIN
Ian Lo Leong Ting, Nafis Ul Islam, Yoko Lau Tsz Ching
Background
Robotic arms have been widely used in various real-world scenarios, such as automobile manufacturing and housekeeping. However, there is a significant gap at the Innovation Wing, as existing robotics-focused projects mainly focus on mobile robots or quadrupeds. To address this gap, our project aims to develop an intelligent manipulator capable of performing precise tasks like maintenance and part sorting in industrial settings.
Potentials
Enables operators to remotely monitor the real arm's performance in real-time, ensuring human presence is minimized in potentially dangerous areas.
Provides a safe environment for planning and testing operations before execution.
Facilitates efficient decision-making through simulation, machine learning, and reasoning.
Visualization Results
Our ROS package includes visualization capabilities using RViz, enabling users to observe the robotic arm's movement and behaviour in real-time.
We continuously update the step-by-step teaching materials, empowering users to effectively learn and understand complex robotic arm controls through hands-on experiments.
"A digital twin is a virtual representation of an object or system designed to reflect a physical object accurately. It is updated from real-time data and uses simulation, machine learning and reasoning to help make decisions." -- IBM

Process

Key Features
Versatile Control:
Our package offers various control methods, including:
Joystick control for precise end-effector coordinate manipulation
Sliding bar control for accurate joint angle adjustment
Click & Go interaction for seamless positioning.
Leader-Follower Capability: allows either the physical or the simulated arm to take the lead, while the other arm acts as a follower. This flexibility enables collaborative tasks, where the digital arm can guide the physical arm's movements or vice versa.
ROS
NOETIC NINJEMYS
README
DOBOT Magician ROS Controllers
This is a digital twin ROS package for the DOBOT Magician robotic arm. It provides a simple interface to control the robot arm. The package has been tested with ROS Noetic on Ubuntu 20.04.
Usage
Steps to run the package:
1. Navigate to this directory in the terminal.
2. Run catkin_make to build the package.
3. Run source devel/setup.bash before running the following commands.
Digital Twin
# Terminal 1
roslaunch magician display.launch
# Terminal 2
# Connect the dobot magician and a joystick to the computer
sudo chmod +x /dev/ttyUSB0 (or /ttyACM0)
roslaunch magician_control joystick-real.launch
Use the joystick to control the real robot arm's end effector coordinate. Can also use buttons on the joystick to home the robot arm and toggle the gripper.
In RViz, press the c shortcut key to enable the Publish Point tool. Click on the green plane to set a target position for the end effector.
The simulation robot arm will be in sync with the real robot arm (two-way joint state communication).

CONCLUSIONS
ChatGPT helped students achieve the learning outcomes in this PBL tutorial, and could help students obtain
factual knowledge and provide clinically relevant suggestions.
While most students agreed that ChatGPT should be incorporated in this PBL tutorial, there are concerns
about the risk of automation bias which could hinder the development of clinical reasoning skills.
Both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.0 models of ChatGPT could achieve the PBL learning outcomes with minimal
prompting.
While the adoption of generative AI in medical education brings promise, this should be done carefully while
considering the skillsets required for future clinicians in the AI era.

Building on its prior achievements in speed and the current maneuverability, the robotic fish has promising practical applications in open seas and represents a significant step forward in the development of agile robotic fish technology.
The biomimetic design does not adversely affect marine life, which sets it apart from other underwater vehicles that utilise turbines. In addition to being highly energy-efficient and less polluting, this model is also environmentally friendly due to its minimal use of materials during construction.
Limitless Underwater Motion Control
The fish achieved full motion control through utilising a Pixhawk microcontroller, which receives user commands for throttle, roll, pitch, and yaw.
These signals are then translated into corresponding commands for the pectoral and caudal fins, which are capable of receiving signals up to a surface radius of 1-2km.
Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
The fish chassis and caudal fin are made of eSUN PLA+ material and coated with XTC-4D to ensure waterproofing.
Stainless steel rods have been used for reinforcement, providing sufficient rigidity to overcome oscillation produced by high-speed travel.
The caudal fin features a flexible component made from a 2mm Polycarbonate sheet.
Advanced heat dissipation capabilities
Capable of dissipating heat generated by a 150W motor and maintain the temperature of the motor shell below 60°C while in operation for half an hour.
We are looking to apply this technology in the following ares:
underwater agriculture

Competition & Goals
Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJI during the summer vacation on a yearly basis. It combines technology and e-gaming competition style, thus being exciting and unconventional.
The path to victory consists of the following steps:
Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and restrictions
Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A 0HP enemy base is a victory for your team.
HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017. We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical experience gained during the preparation and participation process. Our work is divided into technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm development.
Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield
Technical Management
Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of development. It should also regulate the development so that it proceeds in a more orderly way.
The efforts we made this season include:
Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical and methodology knowledge.
Archive system, which governs the naming and organization of development files
Documentation system, which specifies the technical details that can be referred to during development to minimize confusion.
Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design. These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance solidarity.
Algorithm development
To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with computer vision are also favorable.
For software and algorithm design, we also come up with detailed plans before development. The plan is known as software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carried out for fine-tuning.

The Hong Kong population can be divided into two big groups: Chinese and the Ethnic Minorities.
PROBLEM IDENTIFICATION
Since the local Chinese language curriculum focuses mostly on reading and writing, kids often have low confidence in speaking Chinese. This has also been amplified by COVID-19 induced online learning. Hence, kids often cannot execute some daily tasks like navigation in the city or buying groceries due to lack of confidence in spoken Chinese.
EDUCATION FOR ETHNIC MINORITIES
Due to high fees at international schools, the majority of non-Chinese students attend NCS (Non-Chinese Speaking) designated local schools. Although these schools are supposed to help the students with cultural integration, the students up to this day face challenges such as racial discrimination and lack of higher education / work opportunities due to the low Chinese language proficiency.

Develop a VR game that can help the kids to execute simple daily tasks in Cantonese;
Conduct end-user testing and evaluate the potential of VR in Chinese learning using the collected feedback.

SLAM Robot with monocular depth estimation in application
Student name :Tam Yung Yip Supervisor: Dr. C.K. Lee
Abstract
SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) technology, which combines mapping with robot localization[1], can help solve the problem of developing accurate environmental maps for robots in unfamiliar environment. This project aim to construct a robot using SLAM and a monocular camera for depth estimation. The system will be able to map the environment correctly and robustly, determining the robot's location and orientation inside it. Then, the robot is capable to estimate the depth using a deep learning model and pictures recorded by the monocular camera as input for further 3D environment construction.

PID control on the car base control
The PID method, which stands for proportional, integral, and derivative, will be utilized to minimize mistakes in motor speed control.
Proportional gain shortens the control system's reaction time, but if it is set too high, the system may become unstable. Integral gain can be aggregated with each speed increase to reduce steady-state inaccuracy.
Derivative gain is used to reduce system stress and can dampen the system. The PID algorithm combines these three parameters to provide fast, accurate, and consistent outcomes.

U-Net structure of monocular depth estimation
The U-Net model is commonly utilized in computer vision tasks for depth estimation. It obtains the contour of the picture by extracting features from two same-size upsampling and downsampling layers, which is then processed through the network's encoder and decoder sections with the ReLU activation function[2]. The U-Net model takes a single RGB picture as input and returns a depth map that represents the distance between items in the scene and the camera. It extracts features using convolutional layers and reconstructs the depth map using deconvolutional layers while maintaining spatial information and incorporates global context.

HINCare: An Intelligent Timebanking System for Elderly Care
Team Member: Hu Zhenwei
Supervisor: Prof. Reynold Cheng
In Hong Kong, the number of elderly citizens is estimated to rise to 1/3 of the population (2.37 million) in year 2037. As they age and become more frail, the demand for support services (e.g. providing domestic or escort services) will increase significantly in the coming years. However, there is a severe lack of manpower to meet these needs. Some elderly-care homes reported a 70% shortage of employees. There is thus a strong need of voluntary or part-time helpers for taking care of elders.
We introduce HINCare, an app that encourages mutual-help in the community. HINCare adopts the concept of timebanking, which each user has his/her own account to store the amount of time ("time credits"). Users earn time credits by providing services to others. The user can use the time credits to purchase other services. Moreover, HINCare uses HIN (Heterogeneous Information Network) to recommend helpers to elders. HIN is a huge graph which stores the relationship information among elders, helpers, and NGOs. We use HIN to meet customized needs of the elders and find the best helpers to assist the elders. Our team use HINs and AI technologies for matching elders and helpers. It is based on our recent research results.
HINCare is a cloud-based system. Administrators of elderly care centers use the system through a convenient web-based interface to perform daily tasks (e.g. task assignment, event announcement, and user profile management). No software installation is necessary, and the system is easy to learn and use. The system is generic and flexible, allowing NGOs to join our scheme easily.
HINCare is now downloadable in Apple and Google Play Store, it has been serving more than 2000 elders and helpers in NGOs (e.g., SKH and CSFC). The app is designed with large fonts and spacing for the ease of elder users. The system attracted media attention, and won the Asia Smart App Award 2020 - Merit Award and the Faculty Knowledge Exchange Awards 2021 HKU. HINCare is extended to support Community Investment and Inclusion Fund (CIIF), a government funding agency and its associated NGOs in 2021.

From tracking clusters, we are able to have preventive measures implemented as soon as possible, which undeniably reduces the impact of an outbreak in all aspects. Sewage monitoring has been under the spotlight for being an accurate indicator of a possible spread and hence our team has curated a sensor that effectively detects viruses for monitoring.

How the PERfECT system works?
From viral shedding of an infected person, parts of the virus, such as the nucleocapsid protein, are present in the sewage sample. As the DNA aptamers on the electrochemical transistor catch these target proteins, PERfECT will transmit data through BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy), to a network coordination point, which will transmit the data wirelessly to the cloud. Authorities can be notified in around 10 minutes from when the virus is detected. Thus, authorities can quickly implement the measures needed and decrease the likelihood of an uncontrolled outbreak.

Objectives
Enhance manoeuvrability to navigate through real-world terrains
Improve waterproofing technique for continuous deployment in water bodies
Increase robustness and efficiency of mechanical/electrical system
Increase controllability by providing better user experience
Swimming across the harbour from Central to TST, our robotic fish will prove its applicability in seawater.
Along with its previous speed record and additional features, it can be beneficial to our society. For instance, its biomimetic nature doesn't interfere with marine life like other underwater vehicles with turbines.
Not only is the new model much more energy efficient, less polluting, but it is also environmentally friendly as it is constructed with less material.
Limitless Underwater Motion Control
The robot consists of 3 main control protocols: the Roll, Pitch and Yaw.
We have developed full motion control of the robotic fish with the aid of Motor Feedback system and PID control of the high-torque servo motor. A DIY controller with simply input from joysticks and a potentiometer is developed to provide accurate and quick control of the robot. With the aid of a suitable configuration for our RC set-up, we have achieve a range of 10m for communication.
Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
Mimicking a fish-like streamlined shape, the drag from the surrounding water current is reduced.
With a new, specialized design, we are able to achieve 100% waterproofing with 3D printing only.
The reinforcement with stainless steel rods has given us sufficient rigidity to overcome the oscillation produced by high-speed travelling.
The complex bearing system at the tail section has ensured a smooth motion with a very low energy loss.
From the previous testing, our chassis is certified to be completely waterproofed for at least 24 hours, while also being able to support the fish for a service time of at least 2 months.

The main aim of this training course is to equip students with practical experience and a general exposure to (i) manufacturing processes, (ii) product design, and (iii) system development. The training course includes a number of modules, covering areas such as design practice, manufacturing technology, measurement, quality control, assembly technology, inspection, troubleshooting, testing, and modification, health and safety, and environmental issues. These modules are designed to motivate students to use creative thinking in the projects, which help them become innovative and open-minded in solving engineering problems.
Ultrasonic sensor is used to provide feedback to the robot for obstacle avoidance. It emits an ultrasound wave and reflect when it hit an obstacle. The received ultrasound wave will generate an digital signal for the on board computer to determine whether there is an obstacle to avoid.
Line-follower sensor is used to guide the robot following a pre-defined pathway. As black object could absorb infrared light, by placing two infrared light LEDs and infrared receivers side by side, we could use them to detect whether the robot is following the "black" path.
Jansen's linkage is a planar leg mechanism designed by the kinetic sculptor Theo Jansen to generate a smooth walking motion. Jansen has used his mechanism in a variety of kinetic sculptures which are known as Strandbeesten (Dutch for "beach beasts"). Jansen's linkage bears artistic as well as mechanical merit for its simulation of organic walking motion using a simple rotary input. These leg mechanisms have applications in mobile robotics and in gait analysis.

iGEM
Problem
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a phenomenon arising from the indiscriminate use of antibiotics and other antimicrobial compounds. Harmful microbes acquire resistance genes that grant them immunity when exposed to antimicrobials. This has led to the concerning emergence of drug resistant bacteria or "superbugs". The WHO declared AMR to be in the "top 10 global public health threats facing humanity".
However, the risk from this menacing phenomenon is not restricted to human health. It is a threat to the environment and environment-dependent industries such as the food industry, which predicts massive production, economic losses, and food safety concerns.
The effects of AMR can be observed on a local scale as well within the Pearl River Delta. In Hong Kong, resistance surveillance in food done between December 2019 and June 2020 revealed that out of the 851 raw beef, chicken, and pork samples tested, 80.1% tested positive for resistant strains. Similarly, out of the 304 samples of vegetable salad, salmon sashimi, and tuna sashimi tested, 15.1% were positive for resistant strains.
AMPed - Our Solution
Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs)
Addressing the challenge of superbugs and meeting the demand for alternatives are a class of compounds called Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs). AMPs are innate defense proteins that have broad-spectrum antimicrobial with high targeting specificity, due to their ability to distinguish pathogenic cell membranes from host cell membranes. Most importantly AMPs are significantly more difficult to develop resistance towards. Our AMP of interest Cecropin B hails from the Cecropia moth and has proven to be highly and broadly effective against microbial pathogens
Microalgae
To complement our powerful AMP, our chassis of choice eventually led to Chlorella vulgaris var. autotrophica. Its low susceptibility to AMPs and efficient expression of complex proteins made it an ideal chassis for the expression of Cecropin B. Compounding Chlorella's known high growth rate, low maintenance cost and straightforward culturing as well as a high nutritional value to the consuming species, it has potential for application as a fish feed supplement in aquaculture, agriculture and even human consumption.
Two-Pronged Application
AMPed integrates Cecropin B and Chlorella into two potent applications: The Secretion Model uses Chlorella as a protein factory, producing Cecropin B in high quantities to be purified for a multitude of downstream uses. The Encapsulation Model takes advantage of the nutrition and robustness of Chlorella to carry Cecropin B internally as a capsule which can convey passive immunity through a supplement or feed product.
Expansion plans
While project can be expanded upon with little effort and minimal financial strain, there is still work to be done. The completed product needs extensive laboratory testing to ensure maximal nutritional value and antimicrobial effect. The production pipeline needs to be streamlined to ensure fast and efficient manufacturing. Field trials also need to be conducted to witness the Chlorella in action in a real world setting so that inputs can be obtained from end users to make final adjustments to suit the needs of the consumers. The project must be also scaled up to industrial levels to meet demands from the markets.

First Prize Project
RoboMaster Sim2Real 2022 Challenge
About the project
RoboMaster Sim2Real Challenge is a robotic competition in which each team designs algorithms for an AI-driven confrontational robot to accomplish two tasks:
1. activate five target objects in the battle field
2. fight with an enemy robot.
Participants are allowed to conduct experiments in a simulator, while direct access to the real-world robot is forbidden. The submitted algorithms of a team will be deployed for real-world validation by the organizers, which determines the final rank.
Our project combines various task-specifically optimized robotic algorithms with some typical confrontation strategies, and achieved a impressing performance.
Localization
Our localization method is based on Lidar map matching. The robot will consistently recieve Lidar signal of the surroundings, and then use it to locate it self on a static map.
Navigation
A refined A* algorithm is used for path planning and path tracking. When a path is found by A*, we translate it into a series of smooth (cubic) curve and further adjust the speed of turning points w.r.t. the robots physical kinetic parameters.
Decision-Making
Initially, we attempted to explore the possibility of bringing Reinforced Learning to generate actions for the robots. However, due to the complicated confrontational environment and limited resources, we at last chose to use the decision tree. We set up a series of rules for the robot to make decisions, and at each step it will filter out less benefitial points according to the ruls.

Cake decoration with 3D printer
Padmanabhan Kishoth/Lui Wing Ming/Tam Ho Kai/Tam Chun Fai/ Ng Hon Fai
Supervisor: Dr M.M.Y. Choy
Department of Mechanical Engineering
INTRODUCTION
Cake decoration is an art which can take many years to perfect, even for a professional pastry chef.
3D printer technology is a novel creative solution to help bakers master cake decorating skill.
Advantages over the traditional approach include speed and accuracy, so that complex design can be more easily achieved.
This study aims to modify an existing 3D printer to make it compatible to extrude food material to decorate the top and side walls of a Cake.
METHODS
A Rheometer is used to measure the fluid properties and analyse compound chocolate and Nutella for decorating.
nutella
HAZELNUT SPREAD WITH COCOA
An extruder is a component on 3D printer that ejects out materials. Modified extruders are used in form of Syringe paste extruder which prints 2D edible food paste.
Hot melt extruder to print 3D edible chocolate models.
RESULTS
Results reveal that paste extruder can successfully print simple to complicated designs using both Nutella and chocolate icing on the top surface of the cake.
Hot-melt extruder can print 3D compound chocolate using dark and milk chocolate models to decorate both the top and side wall of cake.
Happy Birthday
Combining both one can achieve in decorating the top and sidewall of the cake which could be potential in usage in baking quicker, tasty and more complicated designs for amateur bakers and pastry chefs
ACKNWOLEGEMENTS
We would like to express our thanks to our teachers, Dr Marian Choy, Ms Mable Choi and Dr Match Ko for their continuous support and encouragement.
We would like to express our gratitude towards Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing members in supporting our project and organising 6th Inno Show 2022.

Team member: Wong Ka Ngai, Benny

Introduction
This project aims at developing a Connect
Four AI for STEM education that utilizes a
mobile application and a robotic arm to
play with human opponents. It is hoped
that students' interest in CS and AI can be
aroused by playing with the product.
Hardware
The robotic arm has a servo gripper that
picks from the self-made disc stacker and
places in the board. End-stops are installed
for auto-homing and the Bluetooth module
allows the app to instruct the robotic arm.

Software
Board Detection
The app uses OpenCV to detect the board.
It captures and preprocesses the empty
board images, then utilizes circle detection
algorithm (Hough Circle Transform) to find
the 42 circular slots. After getting the center
coordinates of the 42 circles, HSV color
detection identifies their change of colors,
checking for teal or pink disc.
Connect 4 AI
The unbeatable AI is made using a minimax
algorithm with Alpha-Beta pruning. Given a
Connect 4 state, it traverses a tree with all
possible future states. Tree leaves are the
terminal states and their values are returned
to the root. During search, some branches
are cut off as a better move is available. The
algorithm chooses the move that can arrive
the optimal leaf. Besides playing optimally,
the AI tells player the remaining steps to
lose and gives hint.

Working principle of the detection system
A TENG consists of two dielectric materials and they are connected to a
circuit. When two bodies are brought into contact, triboelectric charges are
induced on the surfaces. After separating the two materials, a potential
difference is induced between the two electrodes. To maintain electrostatic
equilibrium, the electron tends to flow to the other side through the external
circuit and current is induced. In our design, Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)
and nylon brush are adopted. Compared with the traditional design, the
brush-type structure allows deformation such that the surface contact area
increases and facilitates the power generation of TENG. A multi-layered
pattern is also adopted in the design to improve performance. The TENG
can generate 1.912 W in 20 minutes.
Unlike the convention detection systems, the design involved no microprocessor
and sensors. A white Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe is bent into 10-degree to form
a V-shaped structure. Clamped. Both interiors of the caps and the pipe are at-
tached with copper tape for electrical conduction. A steel ball is also placed
inside. When the user exhibits shoulder misalignment, the backpack is tilted such
that the steel ball is rolled to the side due to gravity. The steel ball acted as a switch
and completed the circuit of the system by touching the cap and pipe at the same
time. As a result, the electrical energy generated by the TENG is discharged and
actuates the LED to warn the user. With such a design, the system only consumes
0.32 W and fulfills the power supply of TENG.

DOGS, SINCE THE DAWN OF HUMANITY.
Like dogs, quadruped robots are envisioned to play an inseparable part in urban operations under the new normal. DoggiE aims to become the first industrial-grade quadruped robot developed by HKU, accomplish accolades of the quadruped robot "Spot" at Boston Dynamics, and supplement task forces during emergencies and shortage of manpower, broadening the range of surveillance and minimizing injuries/damage to human resources.
