MANUFACTURING
The latest prototype is 40x20x40mm in size and weighs 1kg. The model comprises a main body framework for accommodating electrical/battery components and 4 legs, each of 3 limbs and 3 joints
A hybrid model of manufacturing was utilized for optimal robustness and weight
3D parts such as limbs were modelled in SolidWorks and printed with Polymaker Polylite material
Part of the body framework comprises Laser cut acrylic sections
A total of 12 Goolsky DSSERVO DS3218MG 20kg Metal Gear Digital Steering Servos are used for the 4 limbs
IMPLEMENTATION OF IOT
The ESP32 module is used as the microcontroller unit, as it contains an embedded Bluetooth module capable of initializing a BLE server and detecting Bluetooth clients (i.e. Mobile devices with our DoggiE application)
The inertial measurement unit (IMU) comprises the Adafruit LIS3MDL+ISM330DHCX feathering, which collects and feeds rotational and positional data into the control system
Simulations were run on the PyBullet physics engine for proof-of-concept of both our backend algorithms (e.g. Walking and auto-balancing) and validation of our mechanical design
FEATURES OF CURRENT PROTOTYPE
WALKING, SITTING, STRETCHING
DoggiE enjoys a wide range of motion, which enables it to perform complex tasks while maintaining balance.
REMOTE APP CONTROL
DoggiE is fully responsive to mobile control and implements the latest IoT technology by utilizing BLE networks.

Introduction & Story
FOOD City PANDA Run! is a 3D Runner Game developed during the course of COMP3329 Computer Game Design and Programming. The game idea is actually drawn from a book-keeping app called Fortune City which applies gamification of personal finance managing. We aim to apply a similar design to food delivery apps such as foodpanda, that the game can be embedded to those apps to meet business objectives as retain current customers and attract new ones.
The background story goes as follows. In 20 AC (After Covid), Hong Kong is under a great depression of economy and food supply. To make ends meet, the player has to take a part-time job as a food delivery guy. However, in today's world, even the slightest mistake can lead people being fired, to make sure all the food reaches their customers intact, the player must avoid all obstacles appearing on their road of delivery...

Technical Specifications and Assets Used
FOOD City PANDA Run! is developed on Unity game engine and used c# as scripting language. All assets were purchased on unity asset store, including Hong Kong Street (for overall game scenes), Japanese School Lunch (for food choices), and Mobile Traffic System (for player car). For sound effect of the game, such as background music and coin collect effects, we referred to some online open source of audio materials. Some sample game scenes and assets are shown below:

Game Logic
1. The player initially has 3 food on the tray for delivery.
2. The player can move Left or Right by pressing ← and →, or A and D, to avoid hitting the obstacles and to collect coins as delivery tips.
3. If the player have a minor or indirect collision (like pushing) with the obstacle, it will push the obstacle away without punishment.
4. The food will drop from the tray if the player hit directly with the obstacle. The number of food that drops depends on how hard the player hit the obstacle.
5. The player fails the game if there is no food left on the tray.

COMP3329 Computer Game Design and Programming
Uni Fighters
大學街大亂鬥
Knock your rivals out the U-Street!
Uni Fighters is a game that we have made for the course COMP3329 - Computer Game Design and Programming. It is a 2.5D fighter game set at the University of Hong Kong, portraying a student who gets into a fight for bumping into his schoolmate. Players will play as a student to fight against the opponent using combat mechanics. The game is made with the goal of acting as a stress reliever for players, as well as providing a medium to explore the campus of the University of Hong Kong.
OH NO! I AM LATE FOR TUTORIAL!
HEY YOU! WATCH OUT!
PONG!
WHY ARE YOU BLOCKING MY WAY...
I AM NOT GONNA LET YOU GO UNTIL I HAVE KNOCK YOU OUT!
Fully Custom Made Models and Assets
We made all models and assets from scratch, including the characters, maps, shaders and particle effects.
Meet Sami and Carol, our original game characters! We modelled and handpainted our custom characters in Blender. Every part of them, including the scarf and the hood, are fully sculpted by us from scratch.
By referencing pictures online and captured by ourselves, we modelled a 1:1 replica of the HKU's U-Street in Blender. We applied royalty-free textures including wood and bricks to make it look more realistic.
With the Unity's default shader, the characters looked bland and plastic-like. Using Unity's URP Shader Graph, we made and applied our custom cel shader to the characters to make them look cartoon-ish and lively.
We added particle effects on impact, such as when the characters are being hit by their opponents and when they land on the ground. They were all made from scratch using Blender and Unity's VFX graph.

Investigation on the feasibility of using completely decomposed tuff as a river sand substitute for concrete production
Lam Arthur Hiu Fai
Department of Civil Engineering, The University of Hong Kong
INTRODUCTION
In light of the unsustainable provision of river sand in Hong Kong and the limitations of existing river sand substitutes, Hong Kong urgently needs to discover new river sand substitutes to meet the growing demand for concrete. Trigger -specific Self-prevention and Preliminary Diagnosis
of Depression using Flash Stimulus and GSR sensor
Presenter: QI Baiqian Tong Anze Supervisor: Dr. W.N. Lee (Ph.D., M.Phil., M.S., B.S.), Associate Professor
Introduction
Depression is a common neurological disorder, from which 7.2% of people are estimated to suffer[1]. Meanwhile, different studies show that undiagnosed depression comprises a large share of all the cases, ranging from 40% to 75%[2]. This disease is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and the economic cost from an untreated patient can be up to $550 USD[3, 3]. On the current pandemic situation with a higher risk of getting depression, a better prevention and diagnosis solution is needed to avoid severer people and economic loss[4, 5]-- the current technologies for prevention and diagnosis such as Questionnaires, Internet Behavioral Guidance, and Biomarkers Imaging. However, lack trigger-specific property. Meanwhile, finding the trigger and solving the problem or offering trigger-based psychotherapy is essential for treatment[6]. On the other hand, most of those technologies are clinical-based and are not available to ordinary people to raise their self-awareness of their mental health. The cost and stigmatization towards the psychologist have impeded people from approaching the professionals to prevent their symptoms from deterioration[7]. This study will discuss a breakthrough idea using flash-stimulus to find triggers and provide a possible solution to ordinary people for trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary diagnosis using a GSR sensor.

Globally, depression is a prevalent neurological disorder and can cause severe economic loss. Besides the direct burden on the health care system, the indirect cost on the undiagnosed patients are substantial[2]. Currently, the prevention and diagnosis technologies lack a way to raise self-awareness and provide trigger-specific solutions [3]. This lacking impedes people from preventing the depression deterioration at an early stage, thus causing more severe people and economic loss. To break down their limitations, we propose a plan to give ordinary people a way to trigger-specific self-prevention and preliminary diagnoses. Using the GSR sensor and the strategy of flash-stimulus, we provide a low-cost but user-friendly plan to help the users know better about their mental status. Similar experiments show that using flash-stimulus to find depression triggers is promising.
In the future, depression' s prevalence is likely to grow[15]. WHO has estimated that by the year 2030, unipolar major depression will become the leading cause of disease burden[17]. So, the research in this part corresponds to the future need and is expected to promote people's livelihood.
GSR sensor
GSR sensor's measurement can reflect the subject's emotional change. The measurand is skin's resistance, which can be affected by the emotional change through the pathway, as illustrated in Figure 1.

Skin Resistance
The previous experiment has shown that sweat secretion is associated with arousal level, or the willingness to move[45, 46]. The higher the arousal level, the more sweat will be secreted and the lower the skin's resistance. Based on substantial research, arousal level and valence can be plotted into Arousal-Valence plane (shown as Figure 2), a common framework used for characterizing emotional experiences[47]. Based on the Arousal-Valence plane, depression is characterized by Low Arousal and Low Valence (LALV), while stress is characterized by High Arousal and Low Valence (HALV). So, we can distinguish these two emotional experiences by the difference in arousal value[48].
Flash Stimulus
Flash stimulus is a procedure of showing the potential trigger to the subject quickly in pictures or sounds. This strategy is similar to Allergen t esting. Allergen testing aims to find the allergen by giving a small dose to the subject and observing the subject's physiological reaction. Our test is to find the depression trigger by giving a flash stimulus about the major depression triggers mentioned in section 1, using pictures like the grade transcript and marriage photo to examine the user's reaction.

Our project operates on a ROS (Robot Operating System)-based codebase. Through collaborative development from existing open-source code, we present a competition-level solution to our robotics. DETECTION
To target the armor of the enemy robots, we deployed an industrial camera and an Nvidia-TX2 AI development board in the car. Considering that the aiming task is sensitive to position information and detection speed, we avoided the traditional use of CNN and used DETR as our automatic aiming baseline. Further development will involve quantifying the model and coupling the detection module as well as the muzzle control module to improve further aiming speed and accuracy.

LOCALIZATION
To improve the robustness of positioning, we use multimodal information (robot-mounted lidar, depth camera, optical camera), which give possible estimates of the current position through their respective data processing programs and simply combine them using the Kalman filter algorithm in the decision making. Further consideration will be given to the collaborative processing of these data.
Figure 3: The multimodal information used by localization
ALGORITHM
We prepared two plans for decision making, one works on the behavior tree, and another is based on Deep Reinforcement Learning. We choose the behavior tree as a demo since the training result is not yet satisfactory.
We also use the heap-optimized A* algorithm to plan the robot's path. To ensure that the car can reach the destination quickly and safely, we mark the dangerous area on the map as high-cost. And we shrink the empty part of the node to speed up the code.
Figure 4: The possible route planned by our A* algorithm
WHAT ARE WE GOING TO DO?
We believe there is something more precious than the prizes of the competition. We are committed to training the team's collaborative development ability and hardware and software coordination ability through RMUA. We want to stimulate students' interest in research and programming and form a community to share their ideas.
